sec06-card-sec06-F080.question_text: Why must you keep van or trailer doors shut if a fire starts in the cargo area?
sec06-card-sec06-F080.teaching_text: Swinging cargo doors open feeds a rush of fresh oxygen that turns smoldering freight into a flashover fireball.

sec06-card-sec06-F081.question_text: Under what two conditions should you even attempt to fight a vehicle fire yourself?
sec06-card-sec06-F081.teaching_text: Vehicle fires release toxic fumes and flare rapidly, so step back unless it is clearly safe and you know the extinguisher.

sec06-card-sec06-F082.question_text: Where should you stand relative to wind and distance, and what part of the fire do you aim an extinguisher at?
sec06-card-sec06-F082.teaching_text: Staying upwind and back keeps toxic smoke off your lungs while sweeping the base smothers the burning fuel source.

sec06-card-sec06-F083.question_text: Why isn't a fire truly out the moment visible flames disappear?
sec06-card-sec06-F083.teaching_text: Superheated rubber, wiring, and oil vapor can flash right back into flame until the underlying material cools completely.

sec06-card-sec06-F084.question_text: How should you evade and warn an oncoming vehicle driving toward you in your lane, and which lane must you avoid?
sec06-card-sec06-F084.teaching_text: Swinging left into the oncoming driver's vacated lane risks a head-on crash right when that driver corrects back right.

sec06-card-sec06-F085.question_text: If your car stalls on railroad tracks with a train approaching, which direction must you evacuate on foot?
sec06-card-sec06-F085.teaching_text: Moving away alongside the rails angled toward the oncoming locomotive keeps you clear of flying wreckage pushed downrange.

sec06-card-sec06-F086.question_text: What three immediate control habits apply if your wheels drop unexpectedly off the pavement edge?
sec06-card-sec06-F086.teaching_text: Jamming the brakes or jerking against a lipped asphalt edge flips or spins cars across oncoming lanes.

sec06-card-sec06-F087.question_text: What three conditions must be met before steering back onto the roadway after running onto the shoulder?
sec06-card-sec06-F087.teaching_text: Waiting until you regain poise at 15 mph or slower and verify clear lanes prevents slingshotting sideways into traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F001.question_text: When steering back onto the pavement from the roadside, what lane boundaries must your car avoid crossing?
sec07-card-sec07-F001.teaching_text: Overcorrecting across a raised pavement lip shoots cars across the centerline or into fast neighboring lanes.

sec07-card-sec07-F002.question_text: How do pavement rumble strips alert a drifting or approaching driver, and what do they warn about?
sec07-card-sec07-F002.teaching_text: Grooved asphalt buzzes your tires and steering wheel to wake drowsy or distracted eyes near edges or hazards.

sec07-card-sec07-F003.question_text: Which six tire or valve-stem defects should you look for during a walk-around inspection?
sec07-card-sec07-F003.teaching_text: Bald tread, showing cords, sidewall gashes, tread separation, mismatched sizes, or cracked valves invite highway blowouts.

sec07-card-sec07-F004.question_text: What two tire-fitment mistakes must you avoid on the same axle or inside wheel wells?
sec07-card-sec07-F004.teaching_text: Mixing incompatible tire types across one axle skews emergency handling, while rubbing tires overheat and burst quickly.

sec07-card-sec07-F005.question_text: What two dangerous failures can a bent or cracked wheel rim cause?
sec07-card-sec07-F005.teaching_text: Pothole-dented rims break the airtight tire bead, letting air escape suddenly or peeling the tire off in curves.

sec07-card-sec07-F006.question_text: What can rust streaks around lug nuts signal, and when should you recheck lug tightness?
sec07-card-sec07-F006.teaching_text: Rust trails around wheel studs warn of fretting loose nuts, and freshly swapped wheels always need a follow-up torque check.

sec07-card-sec07-F007.question_text: How does the manual classify missing lug fasteners, damaged lock rings, and weld-repaired wheels?
sec07-card-sec07-F007.teaching_text: Missing studs overload remaining fasteners, while weld-patched rims crack unpredictably under cornering and pothole loads.

sec07-card-sec07-F008.question_text: What three immediate control rules apply the instant a tire blows out at speed?
sec07-card-sec07-F008.teaching_text: Stomping the brake during a blowout yanks the car violently toward the flat corner; grip tight and coast down.

sec07-card-sec07-F009.question_text: How do you guide and finish your pull-off onto the right shoulder after a tire blowout?
sec07-card-sec07-F009.teaching_text: Signaling right and waiting until speed drops to a near-crawl keeps the shredded tire from rolling off the rim.

sec07-card-sec07-F010.question_text: How far off the road should you position a disabled vehicle, and which vehicle lights should go on?
sec07-card-sec07-F010.teaching_text: Getting all four tires off live pavement and switching on hazard flashers or parking lamps prevents side-swipe impacts.

sec07-card-sec07-F011.question_text: Which three portable warning devices can alert approaching motorists to your disabled car?
sec07-card-sec07-F011.teaching_text: Setting out reflective triangles, flares, or warning lamps extends sight warning well upstream around dark curves.

sec07-card-sec07-F012.question_text: What two simple visual signals on the car itself show passing help that your vehicle is disabled?
sec07-card-sec07-F012.teaching_text: Propping the hood up or tying a white cloth lets police and roadside assistance spot a breakdown immediately.

sec07-card-sec07-F013.question_text: What does right-of-way mean, and what always outranks insisting on your legal turn to go?
sec07-card-sec07-F013.teaching_text: Legal priority never shields sheet metal, so yielding to a mistake-making driver always beats proving a point in a crash.

sec07-card-sec07-F014.question_text: Alongside obeying intersection signs and signals, how must you treat a vehicle that entered before you?
sec07-card-sec07-F014.teaching_text: Letting a car already inside the junction clear first prevents T-bone collisions even when your approach feels clear.

sec07-card-sec07-F015.question_text: Who must you yield to before turning left across oncoming lanes or into a driveway?
sec07-card-sec07-F015.teaching_text: Turning left cuts across both oncoming headlights and sidewalk paths, putting the entire burden to wait on the turner.

sec07-card-sec07-F016.question_text: What must you do before pulling onto a public street from a private road or driveway?
sec07-card-sec07-F016.teaching_text: Sidewalk joggers and main-street cars hold continuous priority over vehicles emerging from private aprons.

sec07-card-sec07-F017.question_text: Even with a steady green traffic light, who must you still yield to before driving through?
sec07-card-sec07-F017.teaching_text: Green grants conditional entry only after late-clearing walkers and turning vehicles finish leaving the box.

sec07-card-sec07-F018.question_text: How must you respond when an emergency vehicle approaches running flashing lights or a siren?
sec07-card-sec07-F018.teaching_text: Clearing promptly to the curb and remaining stopped keeps intersection lanes open for ambulances, police, and fire rigs.

sec07-card-sec07-F019.question_text: How far back must you stay behind fire apparatus responding to an alarm?
sec07-card-sec07-F019.teaching_text: Fire engines stop abruptly at hydrants or swing wide into scenes, making a 500-foot buffer mandatory in DC.

sec07-card-sec07-F020.question_text: May you drive onto a city block where emergency or fire vehicles are stopped working a scene?
sec07-card-sec07-F020.teaching_text: Entering an active fire block tangles supply hoses and traps responders, so turn onto an alternate street immediately.

sec07-card-sec07-F021.question_text: What authorities and signal displays limit a pedestrian's right-of-way at crossings?
sec07-card-sec07-F021.teaching_text: Pedestrians must obey police directions and traffic signals, including waiting when facing a red pedestrian signal.

sec07-card-sec07-F022.question_text: Where pedestrian signals are installed, which signal heads govern walkers versus drivers?
sec07-card-sec07-F022.teaching_text: District intersections frequently run leading pedestrian intervals where WALK lights up seconds before vehicle greens.

sec07-card-sec07-F023.question_text: When must a District motorist come to a complete stop rather than merely slowing for a pedestrian in a crosswalk?
sec07-card-sec07-F023.teaching_text: DC law demands a full stop whenever a walker is on your roadway half or close enough on the adjacent half to face danger.

sec07-card-sec07-F024.question_text: Why is it illegal to pass another vehicle stopped at an intersection crosswalk?
sec07-card-sec07-F024.teaching_text: The stopped car's hood hides a crossing pedestrian stepping straight into your adjacent travel lane.

sec07-card-sec07-F025.question_text: What curb-leaving action does the handbook forbid pedestrians from taking in front of close traffic?
sec07-card-sec07-F025.teaching_text: Physics sets hard braking limits, so walkers may not step off a curb right in front of a close-range bumper.

sec07-card-sec07-F026.question_text: How must a driver react when someone crosses outside a crosswalk without legal right-of-way?
sec07-card-sec07-F026.teaching_text: A walker's lack of legal priority never excuses hitting someone; every driver carries an overriding duty to avoid crashes.

sec07-card-sec07-F027.question_text: Who yields when a walker crosses at street grade despite a pedestrian bridge or tunnel, and what duty stays on drivers?
sec07-card-sec07-F027.teaching_text: Surface crossers near overpasses or underpasses forfeit priority, yet motorists must still exercise care not to strike them.

sec07-card-sec07-F028.question_text: Between two nearby signalized intersections, how does the manual describe crossing the street?
sec07-card-sec07-F028.teaching_text: On dense city blocks framed by traffic lights, walkers cross inside marked stripes or only after yielding to approaching cars.

sec07-card-sec07-F029.question_text: How should you treat pedestrians who are deaf or who travel with service animals or mobility aids?
sec07-card-sec07-F029.teaching_text: Deaf walkers cannot hear engine or horn cues, and guide dogs or canes require unhurried clearance across wide avenues.

sec07-card-sec07-F030.question_text: Around which two groups of people near the street must you stay poised for an immediate stop?
sec07-card-sec07-F030.teaching_text: Young children and anyone appearing disoriented or impaired can wander off curbs without glancing at oncoming lanes.

sec07-card-sec07-F031.question_text: How does the shape of a school-crossing sign differ from a standard pedestrian-crossing warning sign?
sec07-card-sec07-F031.teaching_text: Five-sided pentagons flag school zones specifically, whereas four-sided diamonds warn of standard foot crossings.

sec07-card-sec07-F032.question_text: How do large trucks compare to passenger cars in acceleration, stopping, and cornering?
sec07-card-sec07-F032.teaching_text: Massive cargo weight stretches both acceleration and braking distances while long wheelbases demand extra cornering width.

sec07-card-sec07-F033.question_text: Why do tractor-trailers frequently cruise in the middle lane of a multi-lane highway?
sec07-card-sec07-F033.teaching_text: Holding the center lane keeps two escape sides open while leaving the right lane free for merging and exiting cars.

sec07-card-sec07-F034.question_text: How should you time and execute a pass alongside a tractor-trailer?
sec07-card-sec07-F034.teaching_text: Commit only when a legal passing lane is wide open ahead so you never get trapped beside trailer tires.

sec07-card-sec07-F035.question_text: When may you pull back in front of an overtaken truck, and what must you do with your speed?
sec07-card-sec07-F035.teaching_text: Waiting until the whole cab grill fills your rearview mirror and holding steady speed preserves the rig's braking cushion.

sec07-card-sec07-F036.question_text: Where are the main blind areas located around a large commercial truck?
sec07-card-sec07-F036.teaching_text: High cabs and solid box trailers block sightlines along both flanks, right ahead of the bumper, and far behind.

sec07-card-sec07-F037.question_text: How should you position your car when following behind a large truck?
sec07-card-sec07-F037.teaching_text: Dropping back where you can clearly see the rig's side mirrors ensures the trucker knows you are back there.

sec07-card-sec07-F038.question_text: Why must you switch to low beams when trailing a tractor-trailer after dark?
sec07-card-sec07-F038.teaching_text: Oversized west-coast truck mirrors bounce rear high beams straight into the cab driver's eyes.

sec07-card-sec07-F039.question_text: What two precautions apply when stopping behind a heavy truck on an uphill grade?
sec07-card-sec07-F039.teaching_text: Manual-shift rigs can roll backward several feet as the clutch engages, crushing an unseen car tucked on their bumper.

sec07-card-sec07-F040.question_text: What should you conclude if you cannot see the truck driver's face in the truck's side mirror?
sec07-card-sec07-F040.teaching_text: Line-of-sight works identically both ways in flat glass, so an unseen driver's face proves you sit inside a blind zone.

sec07-card-sec07-F041.question_text: Why is tailgating closely behind a truck or transit bus doubly dangerous?
sec07-card-sec07-F041.teaching_text: Tucking behind tall rear doors hides you completely from the operator while blocking your own view of hazards ahead.

sec07-card-sec07-F042.question_text: Why must you never dart closely into the space ahead of a moving truck or bus?
sec07-card-sec07-F042.teaching_text: Stealing a heavy vehicle's forward cushion leaves the operator nowhere to shed momentum if traffic suddenly brakes.

sec07-card-sec07-F043.question_text: What rule applies whenever you encounter a large truck reversing?
sec07-card-sec07-F043.teaching_text: Box trailers create a massive blind wall directly astern, so trying to dart behind a reversing rig risks getting pinned.

sec07-card-sec07-F044.question_text: Why do large trucks swing into neighboring lanes to turn, and what curb gap must you stay out of?
sec07-card-sec07-F044.teaching_text: A rig swinging left to set up a right corner looks tempting on the right right before the trailer sweeps the curb.

sec07-card-sec07-F045.question_text: What visibility hazard do large truck tires kick up during rain or slush?
sec07-card-sec07-F045.teaching_text: Eighteen spinning tires throw dense curtains of dirty road mist that instantly coat windshields behind and beside them.

sec07-card-sec07-F046.question_text: Which three equipment items must be ready and active when driving near trucks in wet weather?
sec07-card-sec07-F046.teaching_text: Good wiper blades and full washer fluid cut greasy road spray fast while headlamps keep your car visible in mist.

sec07-card-sec07-F047.question_text: What should you do if making your upcoming turn or exit would force you to cut across a truck's nose?
sec07-card-sec07-F047.teaching_text: Losing three seconds tucking safely behind the trailer beats slicing across 80,000 pounds to catch an exit ramp.

sec07-card-sec07-F048.question_text: On which side does the manual advise overtaking a large truck, and how quickly should you clear?
sec07-card-sec07-F048.teaching_text: A trucker's left mirror offers the narrowest blind spot, whereas right-side passing hides you in the longest No-Zone.

sec07-card-sec07-F049.question_text: How does a tractor-trailer's large size distort your sense of its closing speed?
sec07-card-sec07-F049.teaching_text: Large objects appear to move more slowly than small ones at identical speeds, tricking drivers into risky left turns.

sec07-card-sec07-F050.question_text: How far away must you stop when a school vehicle flashes alternating red lights?
sec07-card-sec07-F050.teaching_text: Lock in DC's exact 20-foot clearance buffer ahead of or behind any stopping or stopped school vehicle flashing red.

sec07-card-sec07-F051.question_text: When may you start moving again after stopping for a school vehicle's red lights?
sec07-card-sec07-F051.teaching_text: Hold your 20-foot stop until the alternating red lamps turn completely off, then roll forward slowly watching for late kids.

sec07-card-sec07-F052.question_text: When is oncoming traffic exempt from stopping for a school vehicle's flashing red lamps?
sec07-card-sec07-F052.teaching_text: Only an intervening physical median or barrier on a divided highway relieves opposite-direction traffic from stopping.

sec07-card-sec07-F053.question_text: Where must you look twice for motorcycles, and why are they so easy to miss?
sec07-card-sec07-F053.teaching_text: A slim single-headlamp silhouette vanishes easily behind windshield pillars, parked cars, and side mirrors.

sec07-card-sec07-F054.question_text: How much of a traffic lane belongs to a motorcycle, and may a car squeeze past inside that lane?
sec07-card-sec07-F054.teaching_text: Riders shift across the full lane to dodge potholes and oil slicks, making same-lane passing illegal and hazardous.

sec07-card-sec07-F055.question_text: Why must you keep generous space when following or overtaking a motorcycle?
sec07-card-sec07-F055.teaching_text: Light weight enables riders to stop and swerve far quicker than heavy cars trailing too closely behind.

sec07-card-sec07-F056.question_text: How does District law treat bicyclists riding on streets compared to motor-vehicle drivers?
sec07-card-sec07-F056.teaching_text: Treat cyclists on DC streets as lawful vehicle operators entitled to travel lanes and governed by traffic controls.

sec07-card-sec07-F057.question_text: How should you expect bicyclists to signal upcoming turns or lane moves?
sec07-card-sec07-F057.teaching_text: Because bicycles lack electric blinkers, watching a rider's arms gives you your earliest warning of a lane move.

sec07-card-sec07-F058.question_text: How should you manage speed, horn use, and lateral space when approaching a bicyclist?
sec07-card-sec07-F058.teaching_text: Blasting a horn right behind a cyclist can startle them into wobbling straight into your path around a pothole.

sec07-card-sec07-F059.question_text: When is it safe to pass a bicycle and pull back into the lane ahead of the rider?
sec07-card-sec07-F059.teaching_text: Wait for wide passing clearance, then merge back right only once you see the cyclist in your rearview mirror.

sec07-card-sec07-F060.question_text: What must you do when oncoming traffic or narrow width prevents passing a bicyclist safely?
sec07-card-sec07-F060.teaching_text: Squeezing past a rider on a narrow DC block risks clipping handlebars; match the bike's pace until space opens.

sec07-card-sec07-F061.question_text: Where may a cyclist position at intersections, and what turning mistake must motorists avoid?
sec07-card-sec07-F061.teaching_text: Passing a cyclist only to cut right directly across their front wheel causes classic urban right-hook crashes.

sec07-card-sec07-F062.question_text: Why should you leave extra following distance behind a Metrobus or transit coach?
sec07-card-sec07-F062.teaching_text: Dropping further back lets you see traffic signals, signs, and brake lights around the bus's wide body.

sec07-card-sec07-F063.question_text: How should you pass a stopped transit bus, and what hazard should you anticipate around it?
sec07-card-sec07-F063.teaching_text: Riders rushing off a bus often step out from its front corner hidden from approaching adjacent-lane cars.

sec07-card-sec07-F064.question_text: How must you respond when a transit bus signals to pull into or out of traffic?
sec07-card-sec07-F064.teaching_text: Giving buses smooth priority entering and leaving curb stops keeps dozens of transit riders moving safely on schedule.

sec07-card-sec07-F065.question_text: May you cut in front of a bus stopped for passengers at an intersection to make a right turn?
sec07-card-sec07-F065.teaching_text: Wrapping a right turn around the nose of a boarding bus puts your bumper straight across unseen alighting passengers.

sec07-card-sec07-F066.question_text: What minimum fine does the District handbook list for illegally turning right in front of a stopped passenger bus?
sec07-card-sec07-F066.teaching_text: Memorize DC's steep $200-minimum penalty for cutting right ahead of a stopped bus, as it is a signature local exam figure.

sec07-card-sec07-F067.question_text: What pavement color and lettering mark a dedicated bus lane in the District?
sec07-card-sec07-F067.teaching_text: Bright red asphalt stenciled Bus Only warns private motorists immediately not to cruise or park in transit corridors.

sec07-card-sec07-F068.question_text: Are District bus lanes active on identical schedules everywhere, and how do you tell when rules apply?
sec07-card-sec07-F068.teaching_text: Some corridors run 24/7 while others cover peak rush windows, so check curbside signs for posted days and times.

sec07-card-sec07-F069.question_text: Which four categories of users may lawfully travel in DC bus lanes without risking a ticket?
sec07-card-sec07-F069.teaching_text: Camera and police enforcement tickets unauthorized private cars while keeping red lanes clear for transit, cyclists, paratransit, and responders.

sec07-card-sec07-F070.question_text: Where no sign specifies otherwise, within what distance of an intersection may you enter a bus lane to turn right?
sec07-card-sec07-F070.teaching_text: Entering earlier than 40 feet without sign permission counts as unlawful bus-lane travel on District cameras.

sec07-card-sec07-F071.question_text: Before merging across a bus lane for a right turn, who must you check for and yield to?
sec07-card-sec07-F071.teaching_text: Bicyclists and express buses roll briskly down open red lanes right beside slowed general traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F072.question_text: What does an illuminated vertical bar on a dedicated bus-only signal allow?
sec07-card-sec07-F072.teaching_text: Do not mistake a white vertical transit bar for a general green bulb because it clears only the bus ahead of traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F073.question_text: How do the three-second flashing triangle and horizontal bar work on a bus-priority signal?
sec07-card-sec07-F073.teaching_text: Just like yellow-to-red for cars, a three-second flashing triangle warns bus priority is closing before the horizontal stop bar.

sec07-card-sec07-F074.question_text: What traffic advantage does bus queue-jump signaling create at an intersection?
sec07-card-sec07-F074.teaching_text: Giving the bus a brief early window lets it pull cleanly ahead of queued cars without fighting a post-intersection merge.

sec07-card-sec07-F075.question_text: How does a DC streetcar travel, and can it share lanes with regular motor vehicles?
sec07-card-sec07-F075.teaching_text: Because streetcars ride fixed steel rails in shared traffic lanes, they cannot swerve around double-parked or drifting cars.

sec07-card-sec07-F076.question_text: How do streetcars move with posted speeds, and what must motorists do along streetcar corridors?
sec07-card-sec07-F076.teaching_text: Streetcars travel at posted traffic speeds, requiring alert scanning and strict compliance with corridor lane and turn signs.

sec07-card-sec07-F077.question_text: On which side and with what precaution may you pass a stopped streetcar headed your way?
sec07-card-sec07-F077.teaching_text: Overtake on the left only when clear and creep cautiously in case boarding or exiting passengers step near the tracks.

sec07-card-sec07-F078.question_text: What penalties apply if you stop, stand, or park on a streetcar guideway or beside a platform?
sec07-card-sec07-F078.teaching_text: A rail vehicle cannot steer around a bumper overhanging its guideway, triggering hefty tickets and immediate vehicle removal.

sec07-card-sec07-F079.question_text: How must your vehicle be positioned when parking along a streetcar corridor?
sec07-card-sec07-F079.teaching_text: Tucking every mirror and tire completely inside the solid white parking stripe guarantees passing streetcars clear your bodywork.

sec07-card-sec07-F080.question_text: What two curb rules apply to car doors and double-parking along a streetcar route?
sec07-card-sec07-F080.teaching_text: Swinging a door into a quiet oncoming streetcar or double-parking beside parked cars stalls the entire rail line.

sec10-card-sec10-F001.question_text: Where do you position your car and how do you steer to start a three-point turnabout?
sec10-card-sec10-F001.teaching_text: Starting tight against the right curb maximizes turning space across narrow city streets while scanning both directions prevents broadside collisions.
sec10-card-sec10-F001.must_match_memory_hook: Right edge, roll slow, steer left

visual_sync.text_span: Right edge, roll slow, steer left

sec10-card-sec10-F002.question_text: Where do you halt the first forward arc of a turnabout, and how do you back up next?
sec10-card-sec10-F002.teaching_text: Halting before your front tires strike the left curb keeps your wheels aligned so you can reverse smoothly into position.

sec10-card-sec10-F003.question_text: Once you halt just before the right road edge while backing, how do you finish the turnabout?
sec10-card-sec10-F003.teaching_text: Forcing a tight turnabout in one rushed swing clips curbs or parked cars when a calm extra cycle clears cleanly.

sec10-card-sec10-F004.question_text: Which two speed standards must every driver satisfy at the same time on the road?
sec10-card-sec10-F004.teaching_text: Driving at the posted number during heavy rain or fog can still earn a citation if conditions demand slower travel.

sec10-card-sec10-F005.question_text: Why must you actively manage your speed around anyone already on or stepping onto the street?
sec10-card-sec10-F005.teaching_text: Test questions trap drivers who claim right-of-way excused their speed when someone was already entering the travel lane ahead.

sec10-card-sec10-F006.question_text: When is driving unusually slowly allowed even if it holds up normal traffic behind you?
sec10-card-sec10-F006.teaching_text: Creeping far below normal flow triggers sudden lane changes and rear-end crashes unless hazards or legal rules require slowing down.

sec10-card-sec10-F007.question_text: When does the handbook advise matching the pace of surrounding vehicles?
sec10-card-sec10-F007.teaching_text: Blending with fast commuters never shields you from a speeding ticket once the pack pushes past the legal maximum.

sec10-card-sec10-F008.question_text: What default speed limit applies on District city streets when no other limit is posted?
sec10-card-sec10-F008.teaching_text: Many learners guess twenty-five from neighboring states, making the District twenty-mile-per-hour street default a classic exam trap.

sec10-card-sec10-F009.question_text: What default speed limit governs District alleys and school zones unless signs set another number?
sec10-card-sec10-F009.teaching_text: Tight sightlines in urban alleys and unpredictable child movement near schools leave almost zero stopping margin above fifteen.

sec10-card-sec10-F010.question_text: How do higher impact speeds affect a crash even when something else triggered the wreck?
sec10-card-sec10-F010.teaching_text: Kinetic energy climbs rapidly with speed, turning a minor mistake by another motorist into severe trauma and vehicle destruction.

sec10-card-sec10-F011.question_text: What sign color and shape combination posts the legal maximum speed?
sec10-card-sec10-F011.teaching_text: Confusing regulatory white rectangles with warning plaques leads drivers to treat binding legal caps as optional suggestions.

sec10-card-sec10-F012.question_text: What colors are advisory-speed signs, and what do they tell drivers?
sec10-card-sec10-F012.teaching_text: Engineers calculate curve and ramp speeds for sharp geometry where normal highway pace can skid tires off the pavement.

sec10-card-sec10-F013.question_text: Even though an advisory speed is not a statutory limit, how can ignoring it still break the law?
sec10-card-sec10-F013.teaching_text: Exam questions test whether you realize outrunning a curve warning can violate the reasonable-speed requirement for that hazard.

sec10-card-sec10-F014.question_text: What is a safety zone, and what rule applies to vehicles around it?
sec10-card-sec10-F014.teaching_text: Transit riders and walkers standing inside signed pedestrian islands expect complete physical separation from passing motor traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F015.question_text: How should you adjust whenever people are standing, walking, sitting, or cycling near moving traffic?
sec10-card-sec10-F015.teaching_text: A cyclist swerving around a pothole or a walker stepping off a curb needs instant space and slower passing speed.

sec10-card-sec10-F016.question_text: What does District rule say about coasting in neutral or holding the clutch down?
sec10-card-sec10-F016.teaching_text: Disengaging engine braking on downgrades overheats service brakes and robs you of instant throttle response during sudden hazards.

sec10-card-sec10-F017.question_text: What authority do authorized school-crossing guards and traffic-control officers hold over drivers?
sec10-card-sec10-F017.teaching_text: Live hand commands override green lights and signs to protect schoolchildren and clear jammed urban intersections safely.

sec10-card-sec10-F018.question_text: What minimum sight distance in both directions is required to make a U-turn near a hill or curve?
sec10-card-sec10-F018.teaching_text: Turning across lanes near a blind crest invites a high-speed T-bone crash before oncoming traffic can spot your car.

sec10-card-sec10-F019.question_text: Where at signalized District intersections are U-turns forbidden?
sec10-card-sec10-F019.teaching_text: Out-of-state drivers often assume green lights allow U-turns, making the District ban at signalized intersections a prime test question.

sec10-card-sec10-F020.question_text: What rule governs wearing earphones, headsets, or earplugs behind the wheel, and what exceptions apply?
sec10-card-sec10-F020.teaching_text: Blocking ambient road sound masks sirens, horns, and screeching tires until an emergency vehicle is right on your bumper.

sec10-card-sec10-F021.question_text: What does the handbook state about removing or modifying mandatory vehicle safety equipment?
sec10-card-sec10-F021.teaching_text: Stripping factory mirrors, lights, or restraints compromises crashworthiness and triggers immediate inspection failure or roadside citations.

sec10-card-sec10-F022.question_text: What rule applies to manufacturer-installed emission-control systems on covered vehicles?
sec10-card-sec10-F022.teaching_text: Defeating catalytic converters or exhaust sensors spikes urban air pollution and guarantees failure during mandatory District emissions testing.

sec10-card-sec10-F023.question_text: Who inside a covered passenger vehicle is legally required to buckle a seat belt?
sec10-card-sec10-F023.teaching_text: An unbelted back-seat passenger becomes a lethal projectile during a frontal crash, injuring belted riders in the front row.

sec10-card-sec10-F024.question_text: Can District police pull a car over strictly because someone inside is unbuckled?
sec10-card-sec10-F024.teaching_text: Primary enforcement means officers need no speeding or equipment violation before initiating a traffic stop for unbuckled riders.

sec10-card-sec10-F025.question_text: What fine and point penalty does the handbook list for a District seat-belt violation?
sec10-card-sec10-F025.teaching_text: Unlike jurisdictions that treat belt tickets as non-moving fines, the District adds license points alongside the fifty-dollar penalty.

sec10-card-sec10-F026.question_text: Who carries legal responsibility for making sure passengers wear their seat belts?
sec10-card-sec10-F026.teaching_text: Waiting to shift out of park until every rider clicks in protects both your passengers and your driving record.

sec10-card-sec10-F027.question_text: What documentation is required to qualify for a medical exemption from wearing a seat belt?
sec10-card-sec10-F027.teaching_text: Verbal claims of discomfort never satisfy an officer without signed medical proof detailing why standard belts cannot be worn.

sec10-card-sec10-F028.question_text: Where must a physician's seat-belt exemption certificate be kept when traveling?
sec10-card-sec10-F028.teaching_text: Leaving medical paperwork at home leaves no proof during a roadside stop when an officer checks unbuckled occupants.

sec10-card-sec10-F029.question_text: How should you position an adjustable head restraint before setting the vehicle in motion?
sec10-card-sec10-F029.teaching_text: A restraint left low behind your neck acts like a pivot in a rear-end hit instead of catching your skull.

sec10-card-sec10-F030.question_text: How do airbags relate to wearing a lap-and-shoulder seat belt?
sec10-card-sec10-F030.teaching_text: Airbags deploy at explosive speed expecting a belt to hold your torso back from the inflating cushion.

sec10-card-sec10-F031.question_text: How many inches does the handbook recommend keeping between your chest and the steering-wheel hub?
sec10-card-sec10-F031.teaching_text: Sitting hunched against the wheel puts your ribs directly inside the high-force deployment zone of the driver airbag.

sec10-card-sec10-F032.question_text: Through what age does the manual recommend keeping children in the back seat with proper restraints?
sec10-card-sec10-F032.teaching_text: Back-row seating shields growing bones from front-impact forces and keeps kids safely clear of front airbag deployment.

sec10-card-sec10-F033.question_text: What strict rule applies to placing an infant in front of an active passenger airbag?
sec10-card-sec10-F033.teaching_text: An inflating front airbag strikes the back of a rear-facing infant carrier with enough force to cause fatal injury.

sec10-card-sec10-F034.question_text: What kinds of projects create a work zone, and can the zone itself move?
sec10-card-sec10-F034.teaching_text: Line-painting and utility crews roll steadily forward, catching drivers off guard when cones were absent minutes earlier.

sec10-card-sec10-F035.question_text: Where do work-zone traffic controls start and finish relative to the physical work site?
sec10-card-sec10-F035.teaching_text: Accelerating the instant you pass the last excavator risks hitting flaggers or taper cones still guiding the merge.

sec10-card-sec10-F036.question_text: Which temporary devices and markings guide drivers safely through a roadwork area?
sec10-card-sec10-F036.teaching_text: Reading temporary channel markers early keeps you inside shifted lanes when old painted stripes conflict with active construction.

sec10-card-sec10-F037.question_text: Which warning-sign color normally alerts drivers to roadwork?
sec10-card-sec10-F037.teaching_text: Spotting high-visibility orange from blocks away gives you early notice to scan for flaggers, narrowed lanes, and slowed traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F038.question_text: What hidden traffic surprises should you anticipate when approaching a work zone near a curve or hill?
sec10-card-sec10-F038.teaching_text: Cresting a rise at full speed leaves nowhere to stop if backed-up cars are stacked bumper-to-bumper around the bend.

sec10-card-sec10-F039.question_text: Whose live instructions and which temporary controls must you obey inside a work zone?
sec10-card-sec10-F039.teaching_text: Flaggers see oncoming dump trucks and single-lane alternating flow that regular signs cannot update second by second.

sec10-card-sec10-F040.question_text: What two actions should you take as soon as advance signs announce a closed lane ahead?
sec10-card-sec10-F040.teaching_text: Racing to the cone taper forces a sudden brake-slam merge right where speed limits drop to protect roadside crews.

sec10-card-sec10-F041.question_text: How should you steer and shed speed through roadwork so drivers behind you do not rear-end you?
sec10-card-sec10-F041.teaching_text: Rear-end collisions are the top work-zone crash type when impatient drivers dart between lanes and slam the brakes.

sec10-card-sec10-F042.question_text: How should you handle steel plates, milled pavement, uneven lanes, and shoulder drop-offs?
sec10-card-sec10-F042.teaching_text: Jerking the wheel across wet steel plates or pavement ledges can unsettle tire grip and pull your car sideways.

sec10-card-sec10-F043.question_text: Why must you maintain generous following space and sensible speed inside a work zone?
sec10-card-sec10-F043.teaching_text: Concrete jersey barriers and open trenches box your lane in, leaving braking distance as your only crash cushion.

sec10-card-sec10-F044.question_text: How should you respond when crews, heavy machinery, or one-lane alternating flow halt traffic briefly?
sec10-card-sec10-F044.teaching_text: Creeping impatiently past a flagger into a shared single lane puts you nose-to-nose with opposing traffic or heavy loaders.

sec10-card-sec10-F045.question_text: What handheld equipment do trained flaggers use to regulate traffic through roadwork?
sec10-card-sec10-F045.teaching_text: A flagger paddle holds full traffic-control authority, so rolling past a raised stop face carries serious legal and safety consequences.

sec11-card-sec11-F001.question_text: What kinds of rules do regulatory signs enforce, including inside active roadwork?
sec11-card-sec11-F001.teaching_text: Treating a lowered work-zone regulatory plate like an advisory hint earns steep speeding penalties and endangers roadside workers.

sec11-card-sec11-F002.question_text: What color and shape combination normally marks hazards or unusual conditions in a work area?
sec11-card-sec11-F002.teaching_text: Recognizing an orange diamond instantly tells you temporary construction hazards ahead differ from permanent yellow road warnings.

sec11-card-sec11-F003.question_text: How do cones, drums, and barricades help drivers through roadwork, especially after dark?
sec11-card-sec11-F003.teaching_text: Mounted warning lamps trace temporary lane edges at night when glare and missing paint make shifted paths hard to read.

sec11-card-sec11-F004.question_text: What live updates do changeable-message signs provide to approaching drivers?
sec11-card-sec11-F004.teaching_text: Scanning overhead or portable electronic boards early lets you reroute or slow down before hitting crash backups or event closures.

sec11-card-sec11-F005.question_text: What action does an illuminated arrow board demand, and when can crews run it?
sec11-card-sec11-F005.teaching_text: Waiting until you reach the flashing trailer traps you against cones when adjacent traffic has already packed tight.

sec11-card-sec11-F006.question_text: Which groups of road users must obey traffic-signal indications?
sec11-card-sec11-F006.teaching_text: Every intersection phase assumes walkers, cyclists, and motorists follow their assigned lights rather than improvising turns or crossings.

sec11-card-sec11-F007.question_text: Can you cut through a gas station, parking lot, or shoulder to skip a red light or sign?
sec11-card-sec11-F007.teaching_text: Shortcut drivers darting across corner lots surprise pedestrians and parked shoppers who never expect street-speed cut-through traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-F008.question_text: How are red, yellow, and green lenses normally arranged on vertical and horizontal traffic lights?
sec11-card-sec11-F008.teaching_text: Standardized lens positions let drivers with color-vision differences read stop, caution, and go instantly in glare or darkness.

sec11-card-sec11-F009.question_text: How must you handle an intersection whose traffic signals have gone dark or malfunctioned?
sec11-card-sec11-F009.teaching_text: Blowing through a blacked-out signal at full speed causes devastating cross-traffic collisions when both streets assume priority.

sec11-card-sec11-F010.question_text: Where exact point must you halt for a steady red light, and when may you move?
sec11-card-sec11-F010.teaching_text: Rolling past the white line blocks wheelchair ramps and forces crossing pedestrians to step around your front bumper into traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-F011.question_text: Under what exact conditions may you turn right during a steady red light?
sec11-card-sec11-F011.teaching_text: District intersections frequently post no-turn-on-red plaques, and rolling without a complete stop triggers camera or officer citations.

sec11-card-sec11-F012.question_text: Does the District allow turning left at a red signal?
sec11-card-sec11-F012.teaching_text: Many states allow one-way-to-one-way left turns on red, making the strict District prohibition a favorite exam trap.

sec11-card-sec11-F013.question_text: What does a steady circular yellow light announce to approaching drivers?
sec11-card-sec11-F013.teaching_text: Punching the gas on yellow puts you in the box right as cross traffic launches or red-light cameras trigger.

sec11-card-sec11-F014.question_text: Before accelerating on a steady green light, what must you verify inside the intersection?
sec11-card-sec11-F014.teaching_text: A green light gives permission rather than physical protection if a late left-turner or slow walker is still clearing.

sec11-card-sec11-F015.question_text: When does a green traffic signal NOT allow you to make a specific movement?
sec11-card-sec11-F015.teaching_text: A green ball still forbids turning left or right whenever a companion sign or arrow restricts that movement.

sec11-card-sec11-F016.question_text: What must you do when facing a steady red arrow for your turn direction?
sec11-card-sec11-F016.teaching_text: Even where right-on-red is allowed on circular lights, a steady red arrow holds that movement stopped until it changes.

sec11-card-sec11-F017.question_text: What does a steady yellow arrow signal about your protected turn phase?
sec11-card-sec11-F017.teaching_text: Chasing a fading yellow arrow risks turning straight across oncoming lanes just as opposing traffic gets a green light.

sec11-card-sec11-F018.question_text: How may you move on a steady green arrow, and who still gets priority?
sec11-card-sec11-F018.teaching_text: Protected turn arrows halt conflicting approaches, yet pedestrians or delayed cars already inside the crosswalk still hold priority.

sec11-card-sec11-F019.question_text: How do you treat a flashing red traffic light at an intersection?
sec11-card-sec11-F019.teaching_text: Rolling a flashing red beacon causes T-bone wrecks when intersecting main-street traffic faces only a flashing yellow caution.

sec11-card-sec11-F020.question_text: What must you do when red lights flash or bells ring at a railroad crossing?
sec11-card-sec11-F020.teaching_text: Trying to beat crossing bells or weave around gates leaves zero survival margin against a locomotive needing a mile to stop.

sec11-card-sec11-F021.question_text: Right after the caboose or last railcar clears a crossing, what must you check before driving across?
sec11-card-sec11-F021.teaching_text: A departing train completely hides a second locomotive approaching from the opposite direction on a parallel set of rails.

sec11-card-sec11-F022.question_text: How should you approach railroad tracks that have no gates, bells, or flashing lights?
sec11-card-sec11-F022.teaching_text: Without automated gates or lights, only your eyes, ears, and reduced speed protect you from an approaching train.

sec11-card-sec11-F023.question_text: Why must you never try to beat an approaching train across the tracks?
sec11-card-sec11-F023.teaching_text: Large objects create an optical illusion of slow motion, causing drivers to misjudge closing speed at grade crossings.

sec11-card-sec11-F024.question_text: What does a large painted X with double R letters on the roadway announce?
sec11-card-sec11-F024.teaching_text: Pavement rail markings give advance notice down at tire height even when roadside trees block post-mounted signs.

sec11-card-sec11-F025.question_text: What action is required when you encounter a flashing yellow traffic signal?
sec11-card-sec11-F025.teaching_text: Stopping dead in the lane under a flashing yellow invites a rear-end hit when drivers behind expect cautious movement.

sec11-card-sec11-F026.question_text: How do overhead lane-control signals manage commuter flow on reversible District roadways?
sec11-card-sec11-F026.teaching_text: Morning inbound lanes often reverse outbound for evening rush, so checking overhead symbols prevents head-on wrong-way entry.

sec11-card-sec11-F027.question_text: What rule applies to a travel lane marked overhead by a lit red X?
sec11-card-sec11-F027.teaching_text: An illuminated red X warns that oncoming commuters or closed-lane hazards occupy that strip of pavement.

sec11-card-sec11-F028.question_text: What does an overhead green downward arrow tell you about the lane beneath it?
sec11-card-sec11-F028.teaching_text: Confirming the downward green arrow overhead ensures your direction owns that reversible lane while obeying regular traffic signs ahead.

sec11-card-sec11-F029.question_text: What must you do when an overhead lane-control signal displays a steady yellow X?
sec11-card-sec11-F029.teaching_text: A steady yellow X announces the lane is about to switch to a red X for opposing traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-F030.question_text: What maneuver does an overhead flashing yellow X allow, and who else might enter that lane?
sec11-card-sec11-F030.teaching_text: Using a flashing-yellow-X lane for through passing invites a head-on collision with opposing drivers pulling in to turn left.

sec12-card-sec12-F001.question_text: Why do highway signs use standardized shapes and background colors alongside text or icons?
sec12-card-sec12-F001.teaching_text: Heavy rain, snow, darkness, or sun glare can blur lettering long before a distinct silhouette and hue register.

sec12-card-sec12-F002.question_text: Which four high-priority restrictions or commands do red sign backgrounds and borders communicate?
sec12-card-sec12-F002.teaching_text: Ignoring red regulatory cues puts your vehicle straight into cross traffic, wrong-way ramps, or prohibited lanes.

sec12-card-sec12-F003.question_text: What broad category of message do yellow road signs deliver?
sec12-card-sec12-F003.teaching_text: Spotting yellow ahead tells you to lift off the throttle and scan early for curves, walkers, or school crossings.

sec12-card-sec12-F004.question_text: What type of legal rules appear on white background traffic signs?
sec12-card-sec12-F004.teaching_text: Speed caps and curb parking panels use crisp white backgrounds so drivers recognize enforceable regulations rather than optional guidance.

sec12-card-sec12-F005.question_text: What roadside activity does an orange background sign alert you to?
sec12-card-sec12-F005.teaching_text: Temporary orange panels flag crews, shifted lanes, and maintenance gear where fines and collision risks run high.

sec12-card-sec12-F006.question_text: What navigation information do green highway signs give motorists?
sec12-card-sec12-F006.teaching_text: Reading green destination panels well ahead lets you set up smooth lane changes instead of swerving across exit gore lines.

sec12-card-sec12-F007.question_text: What helpful roadside information do blue signs point out for travelers?
sec12-card-sec12-F007.teaching_text: Knowing blue panels point to fuel, food, lodging, or hospitals keeps your eyes focused on traffic instead of hunting billboards.

sec12-card-sec12-F008.question_text: Which destinations are marked by brown traffic signs?
sec12-card-sec12-F008.teaching_text: In Monument-packed Washington streets, brown panels help sightseers anticipate museum and park turnoffs where tour buses slow suddenly.

sec12-card-sec12-F009.question_text: How many sides does a stop sign have, and what single action does its silhouette demand?
sec12-card-sec12-F009.teaching_text: No other traffic sign uses an octagon, allowing you to recognize a mandatory stop even from behind or covered in snow.

sec12-card-sec12-F010.question_text: What shape is reserved for yield signs, and how must you respond to one?
sec12-card-sec12-F010.teaching_text: Downward-pointing triangles tell you cross traffic holds priority, requiring a full stop whenever safe merge gaps are missing.

sec12-card-sec12-F011.question_text: What message category belongs to diamond-shaped road signs?
sec12-card-sec12-F011.teaching_text: Spotting a diamond outline far ahead cues you to ease off the gas and check for curves, merges, or crossings.

sec12-card-sec12-F012.question_text: What kind of message do tall vertical rectangular signs typically carry?
sec12-card-sec12-F012.teaching_text: Exam questions pair vertical rectangles with speed and lane laws to contrast them against wide horizontal guide signs.

sec12-card-sec12-F013.question_text: What kind of helpful information appears on wide horizontal rectangular signs?
sec12-card-sec12-F013.teaching_text: Separating wide directional boards from tall regulatory plates helps you prioritize mandatory speed and turn laws first.

sec12-card-sec12-F014.question_text: How many sides form a pentagon sign, and what two school locations does it mark?
sec12-card-sec12-F014.teaching_text: Test takers sometimes confuse five-sided school signs with diamond warnings, so picture a classic five-sided schoolhouse roof.

sec12-card-sec12-F015.question_text: What specific hazard ahead is announced by a circular yellow sign with black markings?
sec12-card-sec12-F015.teaching_text: Round yellow signs give early warning well before the tracks, giving you time to quiet the cabin and scan.

sec01-card-sec01-F001.question_text: Which three priorities come together in DC DMV's stated agency mission?
sec01-card-sec01-F001.teaching_text: Every licensing and vehicle rule balances public street safety alongside responsive service for District residents.

sec01-card-sec01-F002.question_text: Into which three main service categories does DC DMV organize its work?
sec01-card-sec01-F002.teaching_text: Grouping citations, driver credentials, and vehicle titles helps residents navigate District DMV centers quickly.

sec01-card-sec01-F003.question_text: What ultimate safety outcome does the District's Vision Zero initiative pursue?
sec01-card-sec01-F003.teaching_text: Vision Zero treats fatal and severe street crashes as preventable system failures rather than routine accidents.

sec01-card-sec01-F004.question_text: Which four building blocks combine inside the District's Vision Zero strategy?
sec01-card-sec01-F004.teaching_text: Pairing crash analytics and safer street layouts with public outreach and policing cuts urban risk.

sec01-card-sec01-F005.question_text: Which two habits define a safe driver among unpredictable road users?
sec01-card-sec01-F005.teaching_text: Expecting sudden errors from nearby cars, cyclists, or walkers gives you space to avoid collisions.

sec01-card-sec01-F006.question_text: Which three personal and mechanical elements make up complete driver fitness?
sec01-card-sec01-F006.teaching_text: Sharp eyes and calm emotions still need reliable brakes, tires, and lights to travel safely.

sec01-card-sec01-F007.question_text: At what point does an everyday cabin activity become a driving distraction?
sec01-card-sec01-F007.teaching_text: Any task pulling eyes, hands, or mind off steering and scanning raises urban crash risk.

sec01-card-sec01-F008.question_text: Which four everyday personal habits inside a car can pull your attention off the road?
sec01-card-sec01-F008.teaching_text: Unwrapping food, checking makeup, or glancing at papers steals vital seconds from urban traffic.

sec01-card-sec01-F009.question_text: Which four device or dashboard interactions are highlighted as driving distractions?
sec01-card-sec01-F009.teaching_text: Tapping map routes, scrolling playlists, or reading texts blinds you across entire city blocks.

sec01-card-sec01-F010.question_text: How can talking with passengers inside your car affect safe driving?
sec01-card-sec01-F010.teaching_text: Lively or heated cabin conversations split mental bandwidth needed to spot crosswalks and brake lights.

sec01-card-sec01-F011.question_text: Which three conditions fall under the handbook's definition of impaired driving?
sec01-card-sec01-F011.teaching_text: Prescription meds and severe fatigue slow judgment and reflexes much like alcohol impairment.

sec01-card-sec01-F012.question_text: What two requirements apply to drivers placed inside DC's ignition-interlock program?
sec01-card-sec01-F012.teaching_text: Covered drivers may operate only breath-tested interlock cars while carrying their restricted credential.

sec01-card-sec01-F013.question_text: Which three personal or intake factors change a person's blood alcohol concentration?
sec01-card-sec01-F013.teaching_text: Rapid drinks on an empty stomach spike blood alcohol concentration faster, especially at lighter weights.

sec01-card-sec01-F014.question_text: Beyond drink count, which five factors can intensify how strongly alcohol affects a driver?
sec01-card-sec01-F014.teaching_text: Mixing drinks with medicine, exhaustion, or emotional stress magnifies impairment even at low amounts.

sec01-card-sec01-F015.question_text: How does the DC manual define drowsy driving?
sec01-card-sec01-F015.teaching_text: Sleep debt dulls hazard recognition, lane tracking, and braking speed behind the wheel.

sec01-card-sec01-F016.question_text: Do rolling down windows or cranking loud music reliably keep a sleepy driver alert?
sec01-card-sec01-F016.teaching_text: Breezes and loud stereos mask tiredness briefly while microsleeps can still strike without warning.

sec01-card-sec01-F017.question_text: How does caffeine compare with proper rest for preventing drowsy driving?
sec01-card-sec01-F017.teaching_text: Coffee gives only a short-lived lift, whereas adequate pre-trip sleep genuinely prevents drowsy crashes.

sec01-card-sec01-F018.question_text: What should you do if drowsiness sets in while you are driving?
sec01-card-sec01-F018.teaching_text: Pulling off to a safe rest spot beats risking a lane departure while sleep-deprived.

sec01-card-sec01-F019.question_text: Which six groups of travelers share space across District streets?
sec01-card-sec01-F019.teaching_text: Dense city corridors mix heavy transit buses and trucks right alongside vulnerable walkers and cyclists.
sec01-card-sec01-F019.must_match_memory_hook: Cars, bikes, walkers, motorcycles, trucks, buses

visual_sync.text_span: Cars, bikes, walkers, motorcycles, trucks, buses

sec01-card-sec01-F020.question_text: At least how many feet of clearance must DC drivers give when passing a bicycle?
sec01-card-sec01-F020.teaching_text: Three full feet gives riders room to dodge potholes without clipping your side mirror.

sec01-card-sec01-F021.question_text: What must you look for before swinging open a parked vehicle's door?
sec01-card-sec01-F021.teaching_text: Opening a street-side door blindly into a bike lane causes severe dooring crashes.

sec01-card-sec01-F022.question_text: Who holds right-of-way when your planned turn crosses a bicyclist's path?
sec01-card-sec01-F022.teaching_text: Cutting right or left across a straight-moving bike lane causes classic right-hook and left-cross hits.

sec01-card-sec01-F023.question_text: How must motorists treat pedestrians, especially at intersections and crosswalks?
sec01-card-sec01-F023.teaching_text: Unprotected pedestrians depend on attentive drivers yielding early at every corner and marked crossing.

sec01-card-sec01-F024.question_text: What is strictly forbidden when another vehicle stops at a crosswalk for a pedestrian?
sec01-card-sec01-F024.teaching_text: The halted vehicle blocks your view of the person walking across into your lane.

sec01-card-sec01-F025.question_text: Where should pedestrians cross streets, and what visibility habit helps keep them safe?
sec01-card-sec01-F025.teaching_text: Crossing at predictable intersections while staying easy to see helps drivers yield on time.

sec01-card-sec01-F026.question_text: Where should pedestrians walk whenever one is provided alongside a street?
sec01-card-sec01-F026.teaching_text: Sidewalks separate foot traffic physically from curb-hugging buses, bikes, and turning cars.

sec01-card-sec01-F027.question_text: How do roadway rights and red-light or stop-sign rules apply to bicyclists?
sec01-card-sec01-F027.teaching_text: Sharing vehicle rights means cyclists also halt at red lights and stop signs like motorists.

sec01-card-sec01-F028.question_text: Which protective gear and roadside hazard check does the DC manual highlight for bicyclists?
sec01-card-sec01-F028.teaching_text: Helmets reduce head trauma while scanning parked cars spots swinging doors before impact.

sec01-card-sec01-F029.question_text: Is riding a bicycle on downtown District sidewalks allowed?
sec01-card-sec01-F029.teaching_text: Busy downtown sidewalks carry dense foot traffic, so cyclists ride on streets or bike lanes instead.

sec01-card-sec01-F030.question_text: How do you perform the Dutch Reach when opening a vehicle door?
sec01-card-sec01-F030.teaching_text: Checking inside and side mirrors before reaching across with your far hand spots approaching bikes.

sec01-card-sec01-F031.question_text: What two physical safety benefits come from opening your car door with the farther hand?
sec01-card-sec01-F031.teaching_text: Swiveling your shoulders naturally points your gaze backward while preventing a sudden wide door swing.

sec01-card-sec01-F032.question_text: How far away from parked cars should a bicyclist ride, with or without a bike lane?
sec01-card-sec01-F032.teaching_text: Keeping three feet clear avoids the full swing arc of suddenly opened car doors.

sec01-card-sec01-F033.question_text: What kind of traffic device is a HAWK beacon, and what is its other name?
sec01-card-sec01-F033.teaching_text: Knowing both HAWK and Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon prevents confusion on DC signs and exam prompts.

sec01-card-sec01-F034.question_text: In what two ways can a HAWK pedestrian beacon be triggered?
sec01-card-sec01-F034.teaching_text: Most crossings use curb push buttons, while select corridors detect waiting pedestrians automatically.

sec01-card-sec01-F035.question_text: How does an activated HAWK beacon create a protected crossing window for pedestrians?
sec01-card-sec01-F035.teaching_text: Halting main-street traffic on steady red gives pedestrians a dedicated WALK interval.

sec01-card-sec01-F036.question_text: How can accessible HAWK equipment alert blind or low-vision pedestrians when WALK begins?
sec01-card-sec01-F036.teaching_text: Sound prompts paired with a tactile vibrating arrow confirm both timing and crosswalk alignment.

sec01-card-sec01-F037.question_text: What traffic control governs drivers emerging from a side street next to a HAWK crossing?
sec01-card-sec01-F037.teaching_text: Overhead HAWK heads face the main corridor, so side-street traffic still obeys its stop sign.

sec01-card-sec01-F038.question_text: What must a pedestrian do first when arriving at a button-activated HAWK crossing?
sec01-card-sec01-F038.teaching_text: A dark HAWK beacon leaves vehicle traffic flowing until the button cycles traffic to red.

sec01-card-sec01-F039.question_text: When WALK illuminates at a HAWK beacon, what should pedestrians verify before stepping out?
sec01-card-sec01-F039.teaching_text: Double-checking halted bumpers protects walkers against distracted drivers missing the red beacon.

sec01-card-sec01-F040.question_text: What should a pedestrian already in the crosswalk do when the HAWK countdown starts?
sec01-card-sec01-F040.teaching_text: Countdown seconds are timed specifically so pedestrians already inside the crosswalk reach the far curb.

sec01-card-sec01-F041.question_text: What should motorists do at a HAWK pedestrian beacon when its lamps are dark?
sec01-card-sec01-F041.teaching_text: Unlike a power-outage intersection signal, a HAWK beacon stays dark until requested by walkers.

sec01-card-sec01-F042.question_text: What does a flashing yellow HAWK indication tell approaching motorists?
sec01-card-sec01-F042.teaching_text: Flashing yellow alerts drivers early once a pedestrian calls the signal before steady yellow follows.

sec01-card-sec01-F043.question_text: How must motorists respond when a HAWK beacon shifts to steady yellow?
sec01-card-sec01-F043.teaching_text: Solid yellow transitions immediately to dual steady red lamps for the pedestrian crossing phase.

sec01-card-sec01-F044.question_text: What must motorists do when a HAWK beacon displays steady red lights?
sec01-card-sec01-F044.teaching_text: Dual solid red HAWK lamps command a full stop while pedestrians have the WALK sign.

sec01-card-sec01-F045.question_text: How do motorists handle the alternating flashing-red phase on a HAWK beacon?
sec01-card-sec01-F045.teaching_text: Treat alternating flashing red like a stop sign, proceeding cautiously only once walkers finish crossing.

sec01-card-sec01-F046.question_text: Which District agency handles questions about HAWK beacons and traffic-control devices?
sec01-card-sec01-F046.teaching_text: DDOT installs, times, and maintains crosswalk signals and street controls across Washington, DC.

sec01-card-sec01-F047.question_text: What is the role of a Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacon at a marked crosswalk?
sec01-card-sec01-F047.teaching_text: Bright strobe-like bars boost pedestrian visibility at multi-lane or high-volume uncontrolled crossings.

sec01-card-sec01-F048.question_text: Where on a crosswalk sign assembly are RRFB light bars positioned?
sec01-card-sec01-F048.teaching_text: Mounting flashers between the yellow pedestrian diamond and downward arrow frames the exact crosswalk line.

sec01-card-sec01-F049.question_text: Which two methods can turn on a Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacon?
sec01-card-sec01-F049.teaching_text: Either pressing the roadside button or walking past passive sensors starts the yellow flashers.

sec01-card-sec01-F050.question_text: What color and pattern do activated RRFB units display to approaching drivers?
sec01-card-sec01-F050.teaching_text: High-frequency yellow flashes grab driver peripheral vision toward pedestrians stepping off curbs.

sec01-card-sec01-F051.question_text: What must motorists do at an RRFB crosswalk whenever pedestrians are crossing?
sec01-card-sec01-F051.teaching_text: District law requires stopping completely for crossing walkers rather than rolling around them.

sec05-card-sec05-F001.question_text: Which four personal conditions form the foundation of safe driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F001.teaching_text: Sharp vision, sleep, drug-free alertness, and physical-emotional steadiness work together every mile.

sec05-card-sec05-F002.question_text: Is holding a DC driver license considered an unconditional legal right or a conditional privilege?
sec05-card-sec05-F002.teaching_text: Because driving is a conditional privilege, unsafe violations can suspend or revoke your card.

sec05-card-sec05-F003.question_text: What criminal penalties can apply to obtaining or knowingly holding a fake license, ID, or learner permit?
sec05-card-sec05-F003.teaching_text: Possessing or applying for fraudulent DC credentials carries serious fines or jail time.

sec05-card-sec05-F004.question_text: How are highway signs tested across both the DC written and behind-the-wheel stages?
sec05-card-sec05-F004.teaching_text: Applicants must identify sign meanings beforehand and demonstrate steady sign compliance during road testing.

sec05-card-sec05-F005.question_text: Into which four sequential mental and physical steps does the DC manual organize driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F005.teaching_text: Scanning first, picking a safe move, signaling others, and steering smoothly keeps traffic predictable.

sec05-card-sec05-F006.question_text: Which guiding principle should determine your driving choice among several possible maneuvers?
sec05-card-sec05-F006.teaching_text: Weighing surrounding traffic and road space lets you select the lowest-risk path every time.

sec05-card-sec05-F007.question_text: Which five visual signals or positioning cues tell other road users what you plan to do?
sec05-card-sec05-F007.teaching_text: Combining proper lane placement with timely lights and hand cues prevents surprises around you.

sec05-card-sec05-F008.question_text: Which five roadway controls or responder commands must DC drivers obey?
sec05-card-sec05-F008.teaching_text: Both fixed street controls and live police or fire-rescue commands carry full legal authority.

sec05-card-sec05-F009.question_text: What should you do when a police officer's hand signal conflicts with a red light or sign?
sec05-card-sec05-F009.teaching_text: Live officers manage crashes, parades, or signal glitches overriding ordinary signs and stripes.

sec05-card-sec05-F010.question_text: May you cut through a gas station or private parking lot to dodge a red light?
sec05-card-sec05-F010.teaching_text: Cutting across corner lots surprises pedestrians near storefronts and violates District traffic law.

sec05-card-sec05-F011.question_text: Which five dangerous behind-the-wheel behaviors exemplify aggressive driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F011.teaching_text: Stacking speed with tailgating, sudden cuts, and red-light violations multiplies multi-car crash risk.

sec05-card-sec05-F012.question_text: Which five traffic or personal pressures commonly fuel aggressive driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F012.teaching_text: Bringing outside stress or running late into city backups tempts drivers into hostile risks.

sec05-card-sec05-F013.question_text: Which three trip-planning mindset habits help prevent aggressive driving before it starts?
sec05-card-sec05-F013.teaching_text: Leaving buffer time or accepting a late arrival beats risking lives to shave two minutes.

sec05-card-sec05-F014.question_text: What speed habit and personal attitude keep you from becoming an aggressive motorist?
sec05-card-sec05-F014.teaching_text: Holding legal speeds while treating other drivers patiently keeps city commutes calm.

sec05-card-sec05-F015.question_text: How should you respond when another motorist tailgates or drives aggressively around you?
sec05-card-sec05-F015.teaching_text: Yielding space and avoiding stares or gestures defuses road rage before conflict escalates.

sec05-card-sec05-F016.question_text: What civic action and passenger example does the manual encourage regarding aggressive driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F016.teaching_text: Alerting police stops dangerous drivers while calm habits teach young passengers lifelong safety.

sec05-card-sec05-F017.question_text: How does District traffic law define reckless driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F017.teaching_text: Knowing danger exists and choosing to endanger people or property elevates carelessness to recklessness.

sec05-card-sec05-F018.question_text: How does negligent driving differ from willful recklessness?
sec05-card-sec05-F018.teaching_text: Even without deliberate malice, inattentive or imprudent handling endangering others violates negligent-driving law.

sec05-card-sec05-F019.question_text: What rule governs vehicle races, speed exhibitions, and drag racing on DC streets?
sec05-card-sec05-F019.teaching_text: Public streets carry unpredictable cross traffic and walkers, making any speed contest illegal.

sec05-card-sec05-F020.question_text: How long must you stop and stay at a crash scene before leaving?
sec05-card-sec05-F020.teaching_text: Driving off before helping injured people and swapping identification turns a crash into hit-and-run.

sec05-card-sec05-F021.question_text: When should you move a crashed vehicle out of active travel lanes?
sec05-card-sec05-F021.teaching_text: Clearing drivable fender-benders off busy travel lanes prevents secondary rear-end pileups behind you.

sec05-card-sec05-F022.question_text: How should you help injured crash victims, and what rule applies to unconscious or severely hurt people?
sec05-card-sec05-F022.teaching_text: Moving an unconscious or spinal-injured victim without training can cause permanent paralysis.

sec05-card-sec05-F023.question_text: Which three details must crash-involved drivers exchange, plus what credential on request?
sec05-card-sec05-F023.teaching_text: Sharing accurate contact, tag, and driver license details satisfies District post-collision law.

sec05-card-sec05-F024.question_text: Where must you report crash details if nobody on scene can receive them and no officer is present?
sec05-card-sec05-F024.teaching_text: Filing promptly with the nearest police station documents your compliance when others are incapacitated.

sec05-card-sec05-F025.question_text: Which three insurance details are included in DC's required crash-information exchange?
sec05-card-sec05-F025.teaching_text: Giving company name, local office details, and policy ID lets claims start without delay.

sec05-card-sec05-F026.question_text: What two steps apply if you strike an unattended parked car or roadside property?
sec05-card-sec05-F026.teaching_text: If you cannot locate the owner nearby, attach clear contact details securely where visible.

sec05-card-sec05-F027.question_text: Whom else must you notify whenever your vehicle is involved in a crash?
sec05-card-sec05-F027.teaching_text: Promptly reporting collisions to your insurer preserves policy coverage and claim protection.

sec05-card-sec05-F028.question_text: Whom must you contact immediately if your vehicle strikes and injures a domestic animal?
sec05-card-sec05-F028.teaching_text: Calling the responsible police agency gets rapid veterinary or animal-control help to the pet.

sec05-card-sec05-F029.question_text: What exterior items and cabin adjustments should you check before starting off?
sec05-card-sec05-F029.teaching_text: Catching low tires, fluid puddles, loose cargo, or dead brake bulbs prevents mid-trip trouble.

sec05-card-sec05-F030.question_text: Which four environmental factors should you weigh before pulling out onto the road?
sec05-card-sec05-F030.teaching_text: Checking glare, storms, slick streets, and rush-hour backups lets you adjust routes and timing.

sec05-card-sec05-F031.question_text: When should you plan a turn and move into the proper turning lane?
sec05-card-sec05-F031.teaching_text: Positioning well before the corner avoids sudden last-second cuts across adjacent lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-F032.question_text: What checks and communication must come before shifting lanes for an upcoming turn?
sec05-card-sec05-F032.teaching_text: Scanning rear and side spaces before blinking keeps bikes and cars out of harm's way.

sec05-card-sec05-F033.question_text: How does slowing for an ordinary street turn differ from taking a highway exit?
sec05-card-sec05-F033.teaching_text: City corners take gradual lane braking, whereas highways shift into deceleration ramps first.

sec05-card-sec05-F034.question_text: How should you check behind your vehicle before backing instead of trusting only the inside mirror?
sec05-card-sec05-F034.teaching_text: Inside mirrors leave low blind zones behind the trunk unless you turn and look directly.

sec05-card-sec05-F035.question_text: At what pace and distance should you reverse, and whom must you watch for?
sec05-card-sec05-F035.teaching_text: Small children sit below trunk height, so keep every reverse slow and brief.

sec05-card-sec05-F036.question_text: May you reverse into or out of an intersection to turn around?
sec05-card-sec05-F036.teaching_text: Backing across intersection crosswalks blinds cross traffic, so use a side street or circle the block.

sec05-card-sec05-F037.question_text: When using a driveway to turn around, which sequence is safer than backing out into traffic?
sec05-card-sec05-F037.teaching_text: Pulling out nose-first gives wide visibility of sidewalk walkers and fast street lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-F038.question_text: For what sole purpose should a motorist sound the vehicle horn?
sec05-card-sec05-F038.teaching_text: Horns exist strictly to prevent imminent collisions with walkers, cyclists, or vehicles, never venting anger.

sec05-card-sec05-F039.question_text: When may you honk inside a Quiet Zone, and what action does honking never replace?
sec05-card-sec05-F039.teaching_text: Leaning on the horn without hitting the brakes wastes vital stopping distance.

sec05-card-sec05-F040.question_text: What stopping and scanning routine applies when pulling out of a driveway or garage?
sec05-card-sec05-F040.teaching_text: Halting before the sidewalk and street catches joggers, strollers, and curb-lane cars.

sec05-card-sec05-F041.question_text: What should you inspect before and during backing out of a driveway?
sec05-card-sec05-F041.teaching_text: Checking behind the bumper first and scanning continuously catches pets, toys, and sidewalk walkers.

sec05-card-sec05-F042.question_text: When should you reinforce electric turn signals with arm-and-hand signals?
sec05-card-sec05-F042.teaching_text: Low sun glare or closely following vehicles can hide flashing bulbs from trailing eyes.

sec05-card-sec05-F043.question_text: What cabin-loading rule governs passengers and packages around the driver?
sec05-card-sec05-F043.teaching_text: Stacked boxes or crowded shoulders restrict steering freedom and create dangerous window blind zones.

sec05-card-sec05-F044.question_text: Which three pet-safety rules apply while driving and when leaving your car parked?
sec05-card-sec05-F044.teaching_text: Loose lap dogs block airbags and steering, while parked cabins turn lethal in heat or cold.

sec05-card-sec05-F045.question_text: Why must loose objects stay off your dashboard and rear package shelf?
sec05-card-sec05-F045.teaching_text: Hard braking or impact launches unsecured shelf items at highway velocity into occupants' heads.

sec05-card-sec05-F046.question_text: Why must water bottles, bags, and floor clutter stay away from the driver's pedals?
sec05-card-sec05-F046.teaching_text: A rolling bottle wedged beneath the brake pedal prevents stopping in an emergency.

sec05-card-sec05-F047.question_text: Which three sudden hazards must you anticipate when driving alongside a row of parked cars?
sec05-card-sec05-F047.teaching_text: Leaving door-zone margin and covering the brake catches people stepping between parked bumpers.

sec05-card-sec05-F048.question_text: At which four road features must you ease off speed when conditions call for it?
sec05-card-sec05-F048.teaching_text: Limited sightlines and side loads at crests, curves, rails, and corners shrink reaction margin.

sec05-card-sec05-F049.question_text: Which five roadside environments or hazards call for reduced speed?
sec05-card-sec05-F049.teaching_text: Tight winding streets and active child zones require low speeds for instant stops.

sec05-card-sec05-F050.question_text: Which three broad conditions can require driving slower than normal travel speed?
sec05-card-sec05-F050.teaching_text: Adjusting speed downward whenever storms, debris, or fatigue arise keeps stopping distance manageable.

sec05-card-sec05-F051.question_text: What kind of slow driving should you avoid when road and weather conditions are clear?
sec05-card-sec05-F051.teaching_text: Crawling far below normal traffic without cause creates bottlenecks and rear-end risk.

sec05-card-sec05-F052.question_text: What two performance losses happen on wet pavement?
sec05-card-sec05-F052.teaching_text: Water film weakens cornering friction while stretching the feet needed to halt cleanly.

sec05-card-sec05-F053.question_text: Why is the start of a rainstorm often slicker than steady rain later on?
sec05-card-sec05-F053.teaching_text: Initial raindrops float dripped oil and grease onto the surface before heavier rain rinses asphalt.

sec05-card-sec05-F054.question_text: How do wet fallen leaves on District streets affect tire grip?
sec05-card-sec05-F054.teaching_text: Matted wet leaves act almost like ice patches under braking or cornering tires.

sec05-card-sec05-F055.question_text: What happens beneath your tires during hydroplaning?
sec05-card-sec05-F055.teaching_text: Water wedges faster than tread grooves can clear it, lifting rubber off the asphalt.

sec05-card-sec05-F056.question_text: What three steps restore grip if your vehicle starts hydroplaning?
sec05-card-sec05-F056.teaching_text: Lifting off the gas smoothly without slamming brakes lets tires sink back onto pavement.

sec05-card-sec05-F057.question_text: How quickly can flash flooding form after heavy rain?
sec05-card-sec05-F057.teaching_text: Low underpasses and creek parkways can flood dangerously inside a single downpour.

sec05-card-sec05-F058.question_text: What must you do when water covers the roadway ahead?
sec05-card-sec05-F058.teaching_text: Never drive into standing water when rerouting or waiting on higher ground keeps you safe.

sec05-card-sec05-F059.question_text: How little standing water reaching a car's underside can stall the engine or cause control loss?
sec05-card-sec05-F059.teaching_text: Six inches reaches many passenger-car intakes and exhausts while floating tires off grip.

sec05-card-sec05-F060.question_text: What depth of moving floodwater can sweep away most cars, pickups, and SUVs?
sec05-card-sec05-F060.teaching_text: Buoyant force inside two feet of current floats heavy trucks and sport-utility vehicles sideways.

sec05-card-sec05-F061.question_text: Why is muddy floodwater dangerous even if the surface looks shallow?
sec05-card-sec05-F061.teaching_text: Murky water conceals collapsed culverts and undermined asphalt ready to swallow front wheels.

sec05-card-sec05-F062.question_text: In the DC handbook's landmark count, arriving before how many seconds means you are following too closely?
sec05-card-sec05-F062.teaching_text: Passing the fixed object before finishing a four-second count leaves inadequate reaction buffer.

sec05-card-sec05-F063.question_text: Behind which types of vehicles should you add extra following cushion?
sec05-card-sec05-F063.teaching_text: Transit buses and mail trucks halt repeatedly at curbs and boxes without long advance runs.

sec05-card-sec05-F064.question_text: How many seconds of following distance does the DC manual recommend in poor weather?
sec05-card-sec05-F064.teaching_text: Expanding your cushion to four or five seconds offsets wet or icy braking lag.

sec05-card-sec05-F065.question_text: Why must you never cut sharply in front of a heavy truck?
sec05-card-sec05-F065.teaching_text: Stealing a truck's front buffer leaves massive cargo weight zero room if traffic slows.

sec05-card-sec05-F066.question_text: Which seven human, mechanical, and environmental variables determine total stopping distance?
sec05-card-sec05-F066.teaching_text: Downhill grades, tailwinds, worn brakes, or delayed recognition all stretch total stopping distance.
