sec05-card-sec05-F067.question_text: How does dwelling on work or family problems affect your driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F067.teaching_text: Daydreaming about personal stress steals cognitive processing from spotting brake lights and walkers.

sec05-card-sec05-F068.question_text: Which three conditions multiply the danger of even a brief cabin distraction?
sec05-card-sec05-F068.teaching_text: Looking away for one second in rain, fatigue, and tight traffic leaves zero recovery margin.

sec05-card-sec05-F069.question_text: Along with grooming, eating, and reading, which two backseat or cabin demands distract drivers?
sec05-card-sec05-F069.teaching_text: Reaching back for falling bags, children, or pets pulls eyes and steering off course.

sec05-card-sec05-F070.question_text: What adjustments and switch checks must you complete before driving an unfamiliar vehicle?
sec05-card-sec05-F070.teaching_text: Hunting blindly for wiper or headlight stalks once rain starts distracts your eyes dangerously.

sec05-card-sec05-F071.question_text: What does drowsiness signal, and how does monotonous highway travel affect road awareness?
sec05-card-sec05-F071.teaching_text: Treating drowsiness as harmless ignores the doorway to sleep while flat highways numb alertness.

sec05-card-sec05-F072.question_text: What action should you take at the very first sign of sleepiness on a highway?
sec05-card-sec05-F072.teaching_text: Pulling into a rest stop immediately for a nap or driver switch prevents microsleep wrecks.

sec05-card-sec05-F073.question_text: Should fatigued drivers rely on stimulant stay-awake products to keep driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F073.teaching_text: Stimulants mask exhaustion briefly before wearing off into sudden, deeper rebound fatigue.

sec05-card-sec05-F074.question_text: Which three physical body cues warn you are getting too drowsy to drive?
sec05-card-sec05-F074.teaching_text: Blurry focus, repeated yawns, and heavy eyelids signal your brain is shutting down.

sec05-card-sec05-F075.question_text: Which four vehicle-handling or memory lapses signal a sleepy driver?
sec05-card-sec05-F075.teaching_text: Forgetting recent miles or wandering across lane stripes means microsleeps have already begun.

sec05-card-sec05-F076.question_text: When tiredness sets in, what two options beat trying to push onward?
sec05-card-sec05-F076.teaching_text: Either napping safely parked or letting a rested companion drive protects everyone aboard.

sec05-card-sec05-F077.question_text: Where must your attention stay instead of grooming, reading, or tweaking entertainment?
sec05-card-sec05-F077.teaching_text: Maintaining a continuous all-around traffic picture catches hazards before they box you in.

sec05-card-sec05-F078.question_text: What should you do before driving if you are upset or angry?
sec05-card-sec05-F078.teaching_text: Strong anger narrows tunnel vision and triggers impulsive speeding or aggressive decisions.

sec05-card-sec05-F079.question_text: What are the two core DC rules on cellular calls and text messaging while driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F079.teaching_text: District law mandates hands-free voice setups and flatly prohibits texting behind the wheel.

sec05-card-sec05-F080.question_text: Which cabin items and dashboard settings should be finalized before shifting out of Park?
sec05-card-sec05-F080.teaching_text: Locking in AC, music, and GPS while parked keeps eyes forward once rolling.

sec05-card-sec05-F081.question_text: How should you handle reading material and complex or emotional conversations on a trip?
sec05-card-sec05-F081.teaching_text: Stashing papers out of reach and waiting until parked for intense talks preserves focus.

sec05-card-sec05-F082.question_text: What should you do if a passenger creates an unsafe distraction while you are driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F082.teaching_text: Stopping in a safe legal spot lets you settle cabin chaos without drifting lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-F083.question_text: How should you handle eating or drinking on a road trip?
sec05-card-sec05-F083.teaching_text: Taking a parked break avoids spilled hot drinks and one-handed steering in traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F001.question_text: Which side of the roadway do you ordinarily drive on, and what two maneuvers create exceptions?
sec08-card-sec08-F001.teaching_text: Staying on the right half keeps opposing traffic separated unless you are actively overtaking or staging a left turn.

sec08-card-sec08-F002.question_text: How much of the usable roadway must you leave for an oncoming vehicle on a narrow or two-lane street?
sec08-card-sec08-F002.teaching_text: Tight rowhouse streets lined with parked cars require easing over so oncoming drivers get their full half of space.

sec08-card-sec08-F003.question_text: For at least how many feet before turning must your directional signal flash continuously?
sec08-card-sec08-F003.teaching_text: Clicking your blinker a last-second car length from the corner fails DC's mandatory 100-foot advance warning rule.

sec08-card-sec08-F004.question_text: How should your turn or lane-change signaling adjust as travel speeds increase?
sec08-card-sec08-F004.teaching_text: At 50 mph you cover 100 feet in barely over one second, so signal much earlier on fast parkways.

sec08-card-sec08-F005.question_text: When your intended driveway or turn sits immediately past an intersection, when should you switch on your blinker?
sec08-card-sec08-F005.teaching_text: Signaling before the cross street tricks waiting drivers into pulling out expecting you to turn at their corner.

sec08-card-sec08-F006.question_text: Which passing side is preferred overall, and where does a one-way street allow passing on either side?
sec08-card-sec08-F006.teaching_text: Left-side passing matches driver expectations, though wide multi-lane one-way avenues safely accommodate passing on left or right.

sec08-card-sec08-F007.question_text: How many lanes must a highway have for the handbook's rule to permit passing on either the left or right?
sec08-card-sec08-F007.teaching_text: Once a highway carries four or more marked travel lanes, lawful overtaking can occur in open lanes on either side.

sec08-card-sec08-F008.question_text: Which two center-line yellow markings forbid passing on a two-lane road?
sec08-card-sec08-F008.teaching_text: Either a double solid yellow center or a solid yellow stripe on your lane edge marks restricted sight distance.

sec08-card-sec08-F009.question_text: What fundamental rule governs oncoming traffic before you pull out to pass?
sec08-card-sec08-F009.teaching_text: If an approaching driver has to brake or hug the shoulder for your pass, you misjudged a forbidden gap.

sec08-card-sec08-F010.question_text: Why are hill crests and blind curves off-limits for passing?
sec08-card-sec08-F010.teaching_text: Rising crests and curving alignments conceal fast oncoming bumpers until closing distance is far too short to escape.

sec08-card-sec08-F011.question_text: Within what distance of an intersection, as well as inside it, is passing prohibited?
sec08-card-sec08-F011.teaching_text: Cross-street cars turning onto the road never expect an overtaking vehicle coming down the opposing lane near corners.

sec08-card-sec08-F012.question_text: How close to a railroad grade crossing does the no-passing ban begin?
sec08-card-sec08-F012.teaching_text: Pulling left within 100 feet of tracks risks getting trapped beside stopping cars or lowered crossing gates.

sec08-card-sec08-F013.question_text: When does approaching a bridge, tunnel, or viaduct make passing illegal?
sec08-card-sec08-F013.teaching_text: Obstructed sightlines within 100 feet of narrow bridge portals, tunnels, or viaducts leave zero shoulder escape room.

sec08-card-sec08-F014.question_text: May you ever drive onto the left or right road shoulder to overtake another vehicle?
sec08-card-sec08-F014.teaching_text: Both left and right shoulders are reserved for emergencies and breakdowns, never high-speed sneaking past traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F015.question_text: Does reaching the end of a marked no-passing zone guarantee it is safe to pull out and pass?
sec08-card-sec08-F015.teaching_text: Broken yellow paint only lifts the statutory ban; you still must verify clear sightlines, weather, and oncoming gaps.

sec08-card-sec08-F016.question_text: Before starting a two-lane pass, what two upcoming limits must you have plenty of room to beat back right?
sec08-card-sec08-F016.teaching_text: You must finish returning to the right lane cleanly before meeting oncoming traffic OR hitting the next solid yellow.

sec08-card-sec08-F017.question_text: What is the safest move if you realize mid-pass that you cannot complete it cleanly?
sec08-card-sec08-F017.teaching_text: Trying to mash the gas to beat closing headlights fails fatally far more often than slowing and dropping back in.

sec08-card-sec08-F018.question_text: When during an overtaking maneuver must you use your turn signals?
sec08-card-sec08-F018.teaching_text: Drivers remember the left blinker pulling out yet forget the right blinker returning ahead of the passed car.

sec08-card-sec08-F019.question_text: How much of the passed vehicle must appear in your rearview mirror before you merge back right?
sec08-card-sec08-F019.teaching_text: Spotting both headlamps centered in your inside mirror proves you have opened a full, safe bumper gap.

sec08-card-sec08-F020.question_text: What minimum clearance must you give when passing a bicyclist in the District, and what horn rule applies?
sec08-card-sec08-F020.teaching_text: DC's strict three-foot buffer prevents mirror clips and wind buffeting, while refraining from honking avoids startling the cyclist.

sec08-card-sec08-F021.question_text: What two obligations apply to a motorist who is being passed by another vehicle?
sec08-card-sec08-F021.teaching_text: Accelerating to block an overtaking car turns a routine pass into a deadly head-on trap in the opposing lane.

sec08-card-sec08-F022.question_text: Under what narrow exception may you pass on the right on a two-lane road?
sec08-card-sec08-F022.teaching_text: You may slip past a left-turning car on the right only if paved roadway width lets you stay off the shoulder.

sec08-card-sec08-F023.question_text: How must your vehicle sit relative to painted lane lines during ordinary travel?
sec08-card-sec08-F023.teaching_text: Straddling dashed lane stripes blocks two lanes at once and triggers side-swipe collisions in tight urban corridors.

sec08-card-sec08-F024.question_text: How many feet in advance does the District handbook specify signaling before changing lanes?
sec08-card-sec08-F024.teaching_text: Don't confuse DC's 100-foot turn signal with its 300-foot advance signal rule for lane changes on test day.

sec08-card-sec08-F025.question_text: Which lane must you choose when driving slower than surrounding traffic on a multi-lane road?
sec08-card-sec08-F025.teaching_text: Keeping slower vehicles in the right-hand lane prevents rolling bottlenecks and risky right-side undertaking.

sec08-card-sec08-F026.question_text: How should you adjust speed and lane position when approaching a vehicle stopped on the shoulder?
sec08-card-sec08-F026.teaching_text: Changing to an open adjacent lane, or easing away inside your lane while slowing, protects stranded drivers and responders.

sec08-card-sec08-F027.question_text: How do you position and signal in advance for a standard right turn?
sec08-card-sec08-F027.teaching_text: Tucking into the rightmost turn lane early with 100 feet of blinker prevents cyclists or cars from sneaking inside.

sec08-card-sec08-F028.question_text: Which two vulnerable groups must you yield to right before turning right?
sec08-card-sec08-F028.teaching_text: Protected and painted DC bike lanes sit right between your passenger doors and the curb where mirrors miss riders.

sec08-card-sec08-F029.question_text: Into which lane of the cross street should you complete a right turn?
sec08-card-sec08-F029.teaching_text: Swinging wide into center or left lanes collides with oncoming left-turners entering the cross street simultaneously.

sec08-card-sec08-F030.question_text: Where must you bring your vehicle to a full stop before making a lawful right turn on red?
sec08-card-sec08-F030.teaching_text: Rolling past the stop bar onto crosswalk stripes before halting fails both road-test examiners and red-light cameras.

sec08-card-sec08-F031.question_text: Which lane and minimum signal distance apply when preparing for a left turn?
sec08-card-sec08-F031.teaching_text: Moving early into the furthest left lane for your direction with 100 feet of signal keeps through-lanes flowing behind you.

sec08-card-sec08-F032.question_text: Which three groups hold right-of-way over a driver making a left turn?
sec08-card-sec08-F032.teaching_text: Drivers fixating on oncoming cars often overlook an oncoming cyclist or a pedestrian stepping into the destination crosswalk.

sec08-card-sec08-F033.question_text: What intersection error must you avoid while waiting for a gap to turn left?
sec08-card-sec08-F033.teaching_text: Getting stranded across cross-street lanes after the signal changes locks up urban blocks and triggers gridlock tickets.

sec08-card-sec08-F034.question_text: Which lane must receive your vehicle at the end of a left turn, and what two errors should you avoid?
sec08-card-sec08-F034.teaching_text: Finishing cleanly in the left lane of your travel side avoids clipping opposing stop lines or drifting into right-lane turners.

sec08-card-sec08-F035.question_text: Does the District handbook allow turning left on a red traffic signal?
sec08-card-sec08-F035.teaching_text: Unlike states allowing one-way-to-one-way lefts on red, DC's manual flatly prohibits turning left against a red signal.

sec08-card-sec08-F036.question_text: What lighting rule triggers automatically whenever you switch on your windshield wipers?
sec08-card-sec08-F036.teaching_text: Daytime rain, sleet, or mist hides gray cars without taillights; turn on real headlamps whenever wipers sweep.

sec08-card-sec08-F037.question_text: In which four driving situations should you run low (dipped) headlamp beams?
sec08-card-sec08-F037.teaching_text: Low beams prevent blinding oncoming or leading motorists and reduce glare under urban streetlamps or dense fog.

sec08-card-sec08-F038.question_text: Between what exact times relative to sunset and sunrise does the District require headlamps?
sec08-card-sec08-F038.teaching_text: Know the exact 30-minute twilight buffer after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise for lighting test items.

sec08-card-sec08-F039.question_text: At what visibility threshold must you switch on headlamps regardless of time of day?
sec08-card-sec08-F039.teaching_text: Heavy storms, smoke, or overcast gloom obscuring people or cars at 500 feet or less triggers mandatory headlamps.

sec08-card-sec08-F040.question_text: What lighting action is required whenever you enter a roadway tunnel?
sec08-card-sec08-F040.teaching_text: Underpasses and District highway tunnels drop ambient light abruptly, requiring active headlamps and glowing taillights.

sec08-card-sec08-F041.question_text: At least how many feet before meeting an oncoming vehicle must you dim your high beams?
sec08-card-sec08-F041.teaching_text: Dropping to low beams by 500 feet keeps oncoming drivers from losing sight of their lane edge.

sec08-card-sec08-F042.question_text: At what following distance behind another vehicle must you switch from high beams to low beams?
sec08-card-sec08-F042.teaching_text: Keep the 500-oncoming versus 300-following split sharp so your high beams never dazzle a lead driver's mirrors.

sec08-card-sec08-F043.question_text: Which three behind-the-wheel driving habits cut unnecessary fuel consumption?
sec08-card-sec08-F043.teaching_text: Jackrabbit starts and hard late stops waste fuel as brake heat, whereas smooth moderate pacing stretches every tank.

sec08-card-sec08-F044.question_text: Which three trip-planning choices help reduce fuel use before you even start the engine?
sec08-card-sec08-F044.teaching_text: Cold engines burn extra fuel on short solo hops, so bundling errands and sharing rides cuts both fuel and congestion.

sec09-card-sec09-F001.question_text: Which four mechanical steps must you complete right after parking on a street?
sec09-card-sec09-F001.teaching_text: Shutting down, locking the ignition, pocketing the key, and setting the parking brake prevents rollaways and opportunistic theft.

sec09-card-sec09-F002.question_text: What three cabin precautions protect your vehicle and belongings before you walk away?
sec09-card-sec09-F002.teaching_text: Visible bags or cracked windows invite smash-and-grab break-ins on city blocks in seconds.

sec09-card-sec09-F003.question_text: Which three vulnerable passengers or companions must never be left unattended inside a parked vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-F003.teaching_text: Closed car interiors trap lethal heat or freezing cold rapidly and leave vulnerable occupants helpless if bumped.

sec09-card-sec09-F004.question_text: How close to the curb must your wheels sit when parallel parked on a two-way District street?
sec09-card-sec09-F004.teaching_text: Leaving tires more than 12 inches off the curb narrows tight DC travel lanes and invites parking citations.

sec09-card-sec09-F005.question_text: What should you do if a close tailgater makes stopping for an open street parking spot unsafe?
sec09-card-sec09-F005.teaching_text: Slamming on the brakes for a curb space with a bumper glued behind you guarantees a rear-end collision.

sec09-card-sec09-F006.question_text: How many feet of side clearance should you leave beside the forward parked car to start parallel parking?
sec09-card-sec09-F006.teaching_text: Starting 2 to 5 feet alongside the front car gives your front bumper room to swing without scraping.

sec09-card-sec09-F007.question_text: Before lifting off the brake to back into a parallel space, what three steps come first?
sec09-card-sec09-F007.teaching_text: Keeping your foot firm on the brake while shifting and turning to scan keeps the car stationary until clear.

sec09-card-sec09-F008.question_text: What path shape and checking habit guide your car smoothly into a parallel parking space?
sec09-card-sec09-F008.teaching_text: Creeping backward along a smooth S-path while alternating front and rear checks protects both neighboring bumpers.

sec09-card-sec09-F009.question_text: Once the rear of your car tucks into the curb space, how do you finish parallel parking?
sec09-card-sec09-F009.teaching_text: Reversing the wheel straightens the nose parallel to the curb, and centering leaves both neighbors room to exit.

sec09-card-sec09-F010.question_text: What should you do if you finish parallel parking more than 12 inches out from the curb?
sec09-card-sec09-F010.teaching_text: Never abandon a car sticking past the 12-inch limit; check traffic, pull out cleanly, and redo the maneuver.

sec09-card-sec09-F011.question_text: Who must you scan for right before unlatching your street-side door after parking?
sec09-card-sec09-F011.teaching_text: Swinging an unlatched door into a bike lane or narrow travel lane causes severe cyclist dooring injuries.

sec09-card-sec09-F012.question_text: What two obligations apply when pulling out from a curb parking space into live traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-F012.teaching_text: Moving traffic already owns the travel lane, so a parked driver must signal and wait for a safe gap.

sec09-card-sec09-F013.question_text: Why is double parking prohibited on District streets?
sec09-card-sec09-F013.teaching_text: Stopping alongside curb-parked cars chokes active lanes, blocks sightlines, and forces sudden lane swerves.

sec09-card-sec09-F014.question_text: How must you secure your transmission and brake whenever parking on a hill?
sec09-card-sec09-F014.teaching_text: Combining Park (or an in-gear manual gearbox) with a firmly engaged parking brake provides dual rollaway protection.

sec09-card-sec09-F015.question_text: Alongside a raised curb, which way do you angle the front wheels when parked downhill versus uphill?
sec09-card-sec09-F015.teaching_text: Pointing downhill tires into the curb and uphill tires away lets the concrete curb chock the front tire instantly.

sec09-card-sec09-F016.question_text: Where there is no curb on a hill, which way do you turn your front wheels uphill or downhill?
sec09-card-sec09-F016.teaching_text: Without a concrete lip to catch the tire, angling toward the shoulder keeps a runaway car off live lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-F017.question_text: When is a vehicle ever excused for stopping on traveled highway pavement, and where should it aim?
sec09-card-sec09-F017.teaching_text: Live freeway lanes forbid parking unless mechanical failure makes rolling impossible, in which case hug the far right.

sec09-card-sec09-F018.question_text: Under what lighting or visibility conditions must a vehicle parked on a highway shoulder run hazard or parking lights?
sec09-card-sec09-F018.teaching_text: At night or whenever visibility drops inside 1,000 feet, glowing shoulder lamps warn fast highway traffic early.

sec09-card-sec09-F019.question_text: What rule governs opening car doors on the traffic side, and what safer option does the manual suggest?
sec09-card-sec09-F019.teaching_text: Sliding across to step out onto the sidewalk side avoids swinging metal doors into fast cars and cyclists.

sec09-card-sec09-F020.question_text: Where do you stop at a stop sign with a painted stop line versus one without a stop line?
sec09-card-sec09-F020.teaching_text: Halt behind the thick white stop bar first; when none is painted, stop ahead of the crosswalk.

sec09-card-sec09-F021.question_text: What kind of stop does a flashing red traffic signal demand?
sec09-card-sec09-F021.teaching_text: Treat every flashing red lens identically to an octagonal stop sign with zero tire roll.

sec09-card-sec09-F022.question_text: Where right-on-red is allowed, what must you do before turning?
sec09-card-sec09-F022.teaching_text: Come to a dead halt first, then yield to crosswalk walkers, cyclists, and cross-street cars before edging right.

sec09-card-sec09-F023.question_text: When does a triangular yield sign require a complete stop?
sec09-card-sec09-F023.teaching_text: Yield never means merge blindly; if pedestrians or approaching cars close the gap, brake to a full stop.

sec09-card-sec09-F024.question_text: What must you do before crossing a sidewalk out of an alley, driveway, private road, or parking garage?
sec09-card-sec09-F024.teaching_text: Blind garage walls and narrow DC alleys hide runners and scooters until you pause ahead of the walkway.

sec09-card-sec09-F025.question_text: When must you hold back before entering an intersection even if your signal is green?
sec09-card-sec09-F025.teaching_text: Entering behind backed-up traffic traps your tail across the intersection and crosswalk when cross traffic turns green.

sec09-card-sec09-F026.question_text: Which two crossing-device states require stopping at railroad tracks?
sec09-card-sec09-F026.teaching_text: Never weave around lowered gates or race flashing red rail beacons; locomotives carry lethal momentum.

sec09-card-sec09-F027.question_text: Outside traffic conflict or officer direction, which three pedestrian or junction zones ban stopping?
sec09-card-sec09-F027.teaching_text: Even brief drop-offs on sidewalks, crosswalks, or inside intersections force walkers into live vehicle lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-F028.question_text: Which two additional curb locations share that strict no-stopping prohibition?
sec09-card-sec09-F028.teaching_text: No Stopping means zero curb pauses even to let someone hop out at public driveways or posted bans.

sec09-card-sec09-F029.question_text: Where is stopping prohibited around a street safety zone unless markings set another distance?
sec09-card-sec09-F029.teaching_text: Keep the gap between a safety zone and the curb clear, plus 30 feet opposite its ends.

sec09-card-sec09-F030.question_text: When is stopping alongside a street excavation or roadway obstruction illegal?
sec09-card-sec09-F030.teaching_text: Stopping opposite a dug-up trench pinches the remaining open lane shut and stalls emergency and transit routes.

sec09-card-sec09-F031.question_text: Which three highway structures prohibit ordinary stopping?
sec09-card-sec09-F031.teaching_text: Zero-shoulder bridges, elevated spans, and enclosed tunnels offer no safe refuge for non-emergency stops.

sec09-card-sec09-F032.question_text: May you pull across to stop facing against the flow of traffic at a curb?
sec09-card-sec09-F032.teaching_text: Crossing opposing lanes to park nose-backward blinds you when pulling back out head-on into oncoming cars.

sec09-card-sec09-F033.question_text: How close to a driveway or alley entrance does DC forbid standing or parking?
sec09-card-sec09-F033.teaching_text: Memorize DC's exact 5-foot buffer beside driveways and alleys so emerging drivers can see sidewalk pedestrians.

sec09-card-sec09-F034.question_text: Within how many feet of a fire hydrant does the District handbook prohibit standing or parking?
sec09-card-sec09-F034.teaching_text: Watch out for state-to-state traps because DC sets fire-hydrant clearance at 10 feet rather than 15.

sec09-card-sec09-F035.question_text: How far ahead of a stop sign, flashing beacon, or traffic signal is standing or parking banned in DC?
sec09-card-sec09-F035.teaching_text: Parking within 25 feet in front of roadside signals or stop signs hides critical controls behind tall vans.

sec09-card-sec09-F036.question_text: Within how many feet of a fire-station driveway entrance is standing or parking prohibited?
sec09-card-sec09-F036.teaching_text: Long ladder trucks need a full 20-foot curb buffer on each side of the bay apron to swing out fast.

sec09-card-sec09-F037.question_text: Where on curves or hill crests is standing or parking prohibited?
sec09-card-sec09-F037.teaching_text: Parking inside a solid-line curve or crest forces trailing cars across no-passing stripes into blind oncoming lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-F038.question_text: What do a No Standing sign and a street-closing barricade prohibit?
sec09-card-sec09-F038.teaching_text: Respect both No Standing zones and closed-street barricades by keeping curb lanes open for transit or work crews.

sec09-card-sec09-F039.question_text: May you stand or park alongside the street side of another vehicle already parked at the curb?
sec09-card-sec09-F039.teaching_text: Stopping double-stacked beside curb cars traps parked motorists inside and blocks live city travel lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-F040.question_text: What limited curb activity is allowed within 50 feet of the nearest railroad rail under the handbook's parking list?
sec09-card-sec09-F040.teaching_text: Within 50 feet of railroad rails, unattended parking is barred, leaving only active loading or unloading of people or goods.

sec09-card-sec09-F041.question_text: What brief curb exception applies at a posted No Parking sign in the handbook's list?
sec09-card-sec09-F041.teaching_text: Unlike No Stopping or No Standing, a standard No Parking sign permits active temporary loading or unloading.

sec09-card-sec09-F042.question_text: Who may lawfully use a designated disability parking space?
sec09-card-sec09-F042.teaching_text: Accessible stalls provide essential ramp clearance and close building access strictly for eligible permit or plate holders.

sec13-card-sec13-F001.question_text: What three-step stopping-point hierarchy applies when you pull up to a stop sign?
sec13-card-sec13-F001.teaching_text: Stopping past a painted line or crosswalk traps pedestrians in moving lanes even if your bumper stays behind the post.

sec13-card-sec13-F002.question_text: Once your wheels stop completely at a stop sign, what must you do before pulling out?
sec13-card-sec13-F002.teaching_text: Treat stopping and yielding as two separate duties so a quick stop never sends you rolling into walkers or cars.

sec13-card-sec13-F003.question_text: What actions and right-of-way checks does a yield sign require before you enter?
sec13-card-sec13-F003.teaching_text: Bicyclists and walkers share full priority with motor traffic at yield approaches, requiring a complete stop whenever space is tight.

sec13-card-sec13-F004.question_text: What legal threshold does a posted speed-limit sign establish for its stretch of road?
sec13-card-sec13-F004.teaching_text: The posted figure sets the ceiling for clean dry conditions rather than a guaranteed safe pace during rain or congestion.

sec13-card-sec13-F005.question_text: What two aspects of curbside stopping can District parking signs limit?
sec13-card-sec13-F005.teaching_text: Urban blocks stack rush-hour tow zones, meter windows, and residential permits that turn a legal spot illegal minutes later.

sec13-card-sec13-F006.question_text: What do overhead lane-use signs tell drivers approaching multi-lane intersections?
sec13-card-sec13-F006.teaching_text: Spotting mandatory or optional turn arrows overhead early stops dangerous last-moment swerves across solid lane stripes.

sec13-card-sec13-F007.question_text: Which vehicles are allowed inside lanes marked by an H O V sign?
sec13-card-sec13-F007.teaching_text: Entering restricted commuter lanes solo during active hours draws steep enforcement fines meant to keep transit moving.

sec13-card-sec13-F008.question_text: What road geometry ahead does a sharp-right-turn warning sign announce?
sec13-card-sec13-F008.teaching_text: Brake before entering a sharp corner rather than mid-turn so front tires keep full grip for steering.

sec13-card-sec13-F009.question_text: How does a right-curve warning sign differ from a sharp-turn sign?
sec13-card-sec13-F009.teaching_text: Distinguishing a sweeping curve arrow from an angled turn symbol helps you match braking smoothly to road curvature.

sec13-card-sec13-F010.question_text: What sequence of bends does a right-then-left reverse-turn warning announce?
sec13-card-sec13-F010.teaching_text: Exiting the first sharp corner too fast leaves your vehicle off-balance right as the pavement snaps back left.

sec13-card-sec13-F011.question_text: What color and shape define most standard warning signs, and how should you react?
sec13-card-sec13-F011.teaching_text: Easing speed at a yellow diamond buys precious reaction distance before you reach the upcoming control or hazard.

sec13-card-sec13-F012.question_text: What response does a stop-ahead warning sign call for?
sec13-card-sec13-F012.teaching_text: Engineers post advance stop warnings before trees, curves, or hills that hide the octagon until late braking range.

sec13-card-sec13-F013.question_text: At an all-way stop intersection, who must halt and which driver goes first?
sec13-card-sec13-F013.teaching_text: Tracking arrival order while rolling up prevents awkward hesitation standoffs and fender-benders inside four-way intersections.

sec13-card-sec13-F014.question_text: How should you drive after passing a signal-ahead warning sign?
sec13-card-sec13-F014.teaching_text: Approaching a hidden traffic light ready to brake prevents panic skids if the phase flips yellow or red.

sec13-card-sec13-F015.question_text: What preparation does a yield-ahead warning sign require as you approach?
sec13-card-sec13-F015.teaching_text: Matching or shedding speed early lets you blend smoothly or halt cleanly if cross traffic fills every gap.

sec13-card-sec13-F016.question_text: What roadway pattern ahead does a winding-road sign warn about?
sec13-card-sec13-F016.teaching_text: Repeated left-and-right bends shift vehicle weight continuously, making early speed control essential before entering the first curve.

sec13-card-sec13-F017.question_text: What conflict point does a side-road warning sign alert you to scan?
sec13-card-sec13-F017.teaching_text: Drivers pulling out from hidden side streets or slowing abruptly to turn off create sudden braking zones ahead.

sec13-card-sec13-F018.question_text: What intersection hazard does a crossroads warning sign announce?
sec13-card-sec13-F018.teaching_text: Four-leg intersections create conflict from both left and right, so cover the brake and check for controls.

sec13-card-sec13-F019.question_text: Where is a yellow no-passing pennant mounted, and what zone does it start?
sec13-card-sec13-F019.teaching_text: Mounting the pennant on the left shoulder keeps it visible even when a tall truck blocks right-side posts.

sec13-card-sec13-F020.question_text: What guidance does an exit advisory-speed sign provide as you leave a highway?
sec13-card-sec13-F020.teaching_text: Highway driving dulls your sense of speed, so checking the speedometer on tight exit loops prevents guardrail run-offs.

sec13-card-sec13-F021.question_text: What specific detail do right-merge and left-merge warning signs reveal?
sec13-card-sec13-F021.teaching_text: Knowing whether ramps join on your left or right tells you which mirror and blind spot to check.

sec13-card-sec13-F022.question_text: Who shares responsibility when a lane-merge warning announces two same-direction streams becoming one?
sec13-card-sec13-F022.teaching_text: Treating a converging lane like a race creates sideswipes when cooperative spacing lets both streams zipper cleanly.

sec13-card-sec13-F023.question_text: What road layout does a T-intersection warning announce, and how must you prepare?
sec13-card-sec13-F023.teaching_text: Missing a T-intersection warning at night risks overrunning the cross street completely because your straight path terminates.

sec13-card-sec13-F024.question_text: What does a small square advisory-speed plate mounted beneath a warning diamond indicate?
sec13-card-sec13-F024.teaching_text: Pairing a hazard symbol with an exact number removes guesswork about how much speed that curve or bump demands.

sec13-card-sec13-F025.question_text: What choice awaits you ahead when a Y-intersection warning appears?
sec13-card-sec13-F025.teaching_text: Deciding your branch early keeps you from straddling the fork or braking hard at the gore point.

sec13-card-sec13-F026.question_text: What roadway split does a divided-highway-begins sign announce, and which side must you take?
sec13-card-sec13-F026.teaching_text: Drifting left of a starting median island puts you nose-first into oncoming one-way lanes.

sec13-card-sec13-F027.question_text: What change ahead does a divided-highway-ends warning announce?
sec13-card-sec13-F027.teaching_text: Drivers accustomed to multi-lane one-way travel often forget the left lane suddenly carries head-on traffic once dividers end.

sec13-card-sec13-F028.question_text: Around what road features does a keep-right sign guide vehicles?
sec13-card-sec13-F028.teaching_text: Channelizing islands and bridge piers sit mid-street, so following the directional arrow avoids curb strikes and wrong-way lanes.

sec13-card-sec13-F029.question_text: How should drivers in both lanes cooperate when a right-lane-ends warning appears?
sec13-card-sec13-F029.teaching_text: Smooth lane drops depend on ending-lane drivers signaling early while through-lane motorists open a courteous gap.

sec13-card-sec13-F030.question_text: What hazard does a steep-hill warning announce, and what system check does it advise?
sec13-card-sec13-F030.teaching_text: Testing brake response and downshifting before a steep descent prevents overheated pads and runaway downhill speed.

sec13-card-sec13-F031.question_text: What cycling activity ahead does a bicycle-crossing warning sign mark?
sec13-card-sec13-F031.teaching_text: Trail crossings and bikeway merges bring fast-moving riders across travel lanes where scanning mirrors and shoulders saves lives.

sec13-card-sec13-F032.question_text: Which vulnerable groups near the pavement edge can a general caution sign alert you to?
sec13-card-sec13-F032.teaching_text: Parkways and neighborhood edges mix runners, pets, cyclists, and strollers just feet from moving mirrors.

sec13-card-sec13-F033.question_text: What three driving adjustments should you make at a slippery-when-wet warning?
sec13-card-sec13-F033.teaching_text: Rain lifts road oil onto wet asphalt, turning sudden steering or hard braking into an instant hydroplane or skid.

sec13-card-sec13-F034.question_text: What does an animal-crossing sign indicate, and during which light conditions must you stay sharpest?
sec13-card-sec13-F034.teaching_text: Deer and Rock Creek wildlife feed actively in low twilight and night hours when headlights barely catch dark fur.

sec13-card-sec13-F035.question_text: What two actions does a pedestrian-crossing warning sign call for?
sec13-card-sec13-F035.teaching_text: Hovering alertly near mid-block and corner crosswalks ensures you halt smoothly instead of skidding toward someone on foot.

sec13-card-sec13-F036.question_text: What maximum speed defines a vehicle wearing a slow-moving-vehicle emblem?
sec13-card-sec13-F036.teaching_text: Closing at highway pace on maintenance gear rolling under twenty-five feels almost like approaching a parked obstacle.

sec13-card-sec13-F037.question_text: What lane arrangement does a two-way-traffic warning announce?
sec13-card-sec13-F037.teaching_text: Transitioning off a one-way urban street into two-way flow traps distracted drivers who linger in the left lane.

sec13-card-sec13-F038.question_text: What maneuver is outlawed by a no-right-turn regulatory sign?
sec13-card-sec13-F038.teaching_text: No-right-turn plaques protect one-way exits, bike boxes, and heavy pedestrian corners where turning right causes direct conflicts.

sec13-card-sec13-F039.question_text: What maneuver does a no-U-turn sign forbid?
sec13-card-sec13-F039.teaching_text: Swinging a prohibited U-turn across tight medians or busy avenues blocks multiple lanes and surprises oncoming traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-F040.question_text: What does a red-and-white do-not-enter sign prohibit?
sec13-card-sec13-F040.teaching_text: Do-not-enter panels guard exit ramps and one-way streets where entering puts you head-on against oncoming vehicles.

sec13-card-sec13-F041.question_text: Which maneuvers require signaling, and when may hand gestures versus electric blinkers be used?
sec13-card-sec13-F041.teaching_text: Notice how the rule pairs hand or electric signals with turns while specifying turn blinkers for lane changes and passing.

sec13-card-sec13-F042.question_text: May you flash your turn signal to wave a driver behind you around to pass?
sec13-card-sec13-F042.teaching_text: Waving a trailing car past with your blinker can lure them into hidden oncoming traffic or mean you are turning.

sec13-card-sec13-F043.question_text: What situation do four-way hazard lamps communicate on a highway or shoulder?
sec13-card-sec13-F043.teaching_text: Flashing hazard lamps alert fast-approaching traffic that your vehicle is disabled or stopped in an emergency.

sec13-card-sec13-F044.question_text: How do bicyclists let nearby drivers know they plan to turn or slow?
sec13-card-sec13-F044.teaching_text: Watching a rider's left or right arm gives you advance notice before they merge across a lane to turn.

sec13-card-sec13-F045.question_text: What shape and color layout identify an interstate highway route marker?
sec13-card-sec13-F045.teaching_text: Recognizing the red-crowned blue shield instantly distinguishes controlled-access interstates from local or United States highways.

sec13-card-sec13-F046.question_text: How does a United States route shield look compared with an interstate shield?
sec13-card-sec13-F046.teaching_text: Telling white United States shields apart from red-and-blue interstate shields prevents wrong-highway turns at busy District interchanges.

sec13-card-sec13-F047.question_text: What colors and shape illustrate a state-route marker in the manual?
sec13-card-sec13-F047.teaching_text: Spotting rectangular state and District route markers helps you distinguish local numbered corridors from shield-marked national routes.

sec13-card-sec13-F048.question_text: Which named freeway corresponds to route DC two hundred ninety-five in the manual?
sec13-card-sec13-F048.teaching_text: Local route-recognition items test whether you connect DC two hundred ninety-five directly with the Anacostia Freeway corridor.

sec13-card-sec13-F049.question_text: Which two signaling methods satisfy the legal requirement before making a right turn?
sec13-card-sec13-F049.teaching_text: If a bulb burns out mid-trip, proper arm gestures keep your upcoming right turn legal and predictable.

sec13-card-sec13-F050.question_text: Alongside right turn and left turn, which third driver maneuver is labeled among manual hand signals?
sec13-card-sec13-F050.teaching_text: Extending your left arm downward warns trailing drivers you are braking even if brake lamps fail.

sec13-card-sec13-F051.question_text: Which leftward movement is named as one of the manual's three driver hand signals?
sec13-card-sec13-F051.teaching_text: Holding your left arm straight out horizontally gives unmistakable notice before turning left across lanes.

sec14-card-sec14-F001.question_text: What three traffic-control jobs do roadway lines, colors, and painted symbols perform?
sec14-card-sec14-F001.teaching_text: Painted lane stripes carry full legal authority alongside post-mounted signs rather than serving as optional visual decoration.

sec14-card-sec14-F002.question_text: What urgent message do red raised pavement reflectors send if they shine back at you?
sec14-card-sec14-F002.teaching_text: Seeing red studs glowing on the pavement at night means you are aimed into oncoming traffic and must back out.

sec14-card-sec14-F003.question_text: Who are parking stalls marked with blue pavement lines reserved for?
sec14-card-sec14-F003.teaching_text: Parking in blue accessible spaces without valid disability credentials blocks vital ramp clearance and triggers heavy citations.

sec14-card-sec14-F004.question_text: How are traffic directions arranged on opposite sides of a yellow center line?
sec14-card-sec14-F004.teaching_text: Keeping yellow paint on your left confirms oncoming cars stay separated, whereas yellow on your right signals wrong-way danger.

sec14-card-sec14-F005.question_text: What passing rule applies along a single broken yellow center stripe?
sec14-card-sec14-F005.teaching_text: Dashed yellow paint permits overtaking from either direction only after confirming plenty of clear sight distance ahead.

sec14-card-sec14-F006.question_text: When a solid yellow stripe runs beside a broken yellow stripe, which lane may pass?
sec14-card-sec14-F006.teaching_text: Always read the stripe closest to your left tire so you never pass blindly where a hill blocks your sightline.

sec14-card-sec14-F007.question_text: When does District rule allow crossing from the solid-yellow side to pass someone ahead?
sec14-card-sec14-F007.teaching_text: Giving walkers, cyclists, and scooter or skateboard riders safe berth justifies crossing solid yellow only when oncoming lanes are empty.

sec14-card-sec14-F008.question_text: What general passing rule do double solid yellow center lines enforce?
sec14-card-sec14-F008.teaching_text: Two solid yellow stripes mark limited sightlines or dense urban corridors where overtaking motor vehicles risks head-on crashes.

sec14-card-sec14-F009.question_text: Which two specific maneuvers may legally cross double solid yellow lines when oncoming lanes are clear?
sec14-card-sec14-F009.teaching_text: Exam questions test whether you know double yellow still allows driveway left turns and safe clearance around cyclists or walkers.

sec14-card-sec14-F010.question_text: What lane setup and driver action does a broken white line indicate?
sec14-card-sec14-F010.teaching_text: White dashes confirm adjacent traffic moves the same way, though mirrors, signals, and blind-spot checks remain mandatory.

sec14-card-sec14-F011.question_text: What two meanings can a single solid white pavement stripe carry?
sec14-card-sec14-F011.teaching_text: Solid white stripes appear near intersections, tunnels, and shoulders where sudden lane weaving creates sideswipe hazards.

sec14-card-sec14-F012.question_text: Beyond lane dividers and edges, which three street zones are outlined with white paint?
sec14-card-sec14-F012.teaching_text: Crisp white transverse and curb markings show exactly where bumpers must halt, walkers cross, and parked cars fit.

sec14-card-sec14-F013.question_text: What must you do if you enter a lane painted solely with a curved turn arrow?
sec14-card-sec14-F013.teaching_text: Driving straight out of a dedicated turn-only lane cuts directly across adjacent drivers who legally turn beside you.

sec14-card-sec14-F014.question_text: What choices do you have in a lane painted with both a straight and a curved arrow?
sec14-card-sec14-F014.teaching_text: Shared option lanes keep urban approaches flexible, provided you signal turns early so trailing drivers anticipate your braking.

sec14-card-sec14-F015.question_text: What do double solid white lines separate, and what is the rule on crossing them?
sec14-card-sec14-F015.teaching_text: Unlike single solid white which discourages shifts, double solid white creates a strict legal wall beside express or special lanes.

sec14-card-sec14-F016.question_text: Where may you pull into a special-use lane bordered by double solid white stripes?
sec14-card-sec14-F016.teaching_text: Designated dashed access zones prevent abrupt speed-differential cut-ins between fast express traffic and slower general lanes.

sec14-card-sec14-F017.question_text: What does a transverse row of painted white triangles across your lane mark, and where does it often appear?
sec14-card-sec14-F017.teaching_text: Halting behind painted yield triangles keeps your front bumper out of circulating roundabout lanes while you wait.

sec14-card-sec14-F018.question_text: On a two-way three-lane road, what does a center lane bordered by single broken yellow dashes allow?
sec14-card-sec14-F018.teaching_text: Because opposing drivers can also pull into a dashed middle passing lane, extreme forward scanning is vital before overtaking.

sec14-card-sec14-F019.question_text: What is a center lane used for when bordered on both edges by solid outside and broken inside yellow lines?
sec14-card-sec14-F019.teaching_text: Using a two-way left-turn lane as a through passing strip invites a head-on wreck with opposing drivers slowing to turn.

sec14-card-sec14-F020.question_text: How far at most may you travel inside a shared center left-turn lane?
sec14-card-sec14-F020.teaching_text: Cruising down a center turn lane past the hundred-fifty-foot limit turns a brief turn pocket into a collision corridor.

sec14-card-sec14-F021.question_text: What painted elements make up a sharrow, and what kind of street lane does it mark?
sec14-card-sec14-F021.teaching_text: Narrow District streets without room for separate bike lanes use sharrows to remind drivers cyclists legally share full lanes.

sec14-card-sec14-F022.question_text: What two practical reminders do painted sharrows give riders and drivers?
sec14-card-sec14-F022.teaching_text: Sharrow placement steers cyclists clear of opening car doors while reminding motorists behind to pass patiently with space.

sec14-card-sec14-F023.question_text: What pavement colors and painted icons identify a preferential bicycle lane?
sec14-card-sec14-F023.teaching_text: Bright green conflict paint and crisp white stripes highlight dedicated cycling space across busy urban intersections and corridors.

sec14-card-sec14-F024.question_text: When may a motorist enter a bicycle lane, and what checks come first?
sec14-card-sec14-F024.teaching_text: Right-hook crashes happen when turning drivers cut across a bike lane without checking mirrors and yielding to approaching riders.

sec14-card-sec14-F025.question_text: Which two types of restricted lanes can a white diamond painted on the asphalt identify?
sec14-card-sec14-F025.teaching_text: Driving solo onto a diamond-marked bus or carpool lane during restricted hours triggers automated or officer enforcement tickets.

sec14-card-sec14-F026.question_text: What details do H O V signs post, and which solo-occupant vehicles may qualify for exceptions?
sec14-card-sec14-F026.teaching_text: Checking exact hours and rider counts prevents tickets while noting exemptions for motorcycles and qualifying clean-fuel vehicles.

sec14-card-sec14-F027.question_text: How are H O V lanes physically or visually separated, and how can barrier-enclosed lanes operate?
sec14-card-sec14-F027.teaching_text: Barrier-separated commuter corridors switch inbound in morning rush and outbound in evening rush behind gated entrances.
